description: Union Government question bank derived from the Constitution of India and parliamentary material. Verify and expand questions before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the office of the President of India?
questions.explanation: Article 52 provides that there shall be a President of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who is the constitutional head of the Union Executive?
questions.explanation: The President of India is the constitutional head of the Union Executive.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article vests the executive power of the Union in the President?
questions.explanation: Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: In the parliamentary system of India, who exercises the real executive authority?

options.B: The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister

questions.explanation: The President is the constitutional or nominal head; the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister exercises real executive authority and aids and advises the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces of India?
questions.explanation: The President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces under Article 53(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How is the President of India elected?

options.B: By an electoral college through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot
options.C: By a joint sitting of Parliament

questions.explanation: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and by secret ballot.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the election of the President?
questions.explanation: Article 54 provides for the election of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who are the members of the President's electoral college?

options.A: Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament only
options.B: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States, Delhi and Puducherry
options.C: All members of State Legislative Assemblies and Legislative Councils
options.D: Only elected members of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The electoral college consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States, and of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and Puducherry.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Are nominated members of Parliament part of the President's electoral college?
questions.explanation: Nominated members of Parliament are not part of the President's electoral college.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Are members of State Legislative Councils part of the President's electoral college?
questions.explanation: Members of State Legislative Councils are not part of the President's electoral college.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article prescribes the manner of election of the President?
questions.explanation: Article 55 prescribes the manner of election of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What voting system is used in the Presidential election?

options.B: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote with secret ballot
options.C: Simple majority in a joint sitting

questions.explanation: The Presidential election uses proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, with voting by secret ballot.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the value of an MLA's vote in the Presidential election based on?

options.A: The number of years the State has been formed
options.B: The population of the State and the number of elected members of its Legislative Assembly, using the constitutional formula
options.C: The number of MPs from the State

questions.explanation: The value of an MLA's vote is based on the population of the State and the number of elected members of its Legislative Assembly, using the constitutional formula; the population figure specified by Article 55 currently refers to the 1971 Census until the relevant figures of the first census taken after 2026 are published.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the value of an MP's vote in the Presidential election based on?

options.A: The total value of votes of all elected MLAs divided by the total number of elected MPs of both Houses
options.B: The population of the State from which the MP is elected
options.C: The number of years the MP has served
options.D: The number of votes cast in the MP's constituency

questions.explanation: The value of an MP's vote is the total value of votes of all elected MLAs divided by the total number of elected MPs of both Houses, subject to the constitutional method of calculation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the minimum qualifications to become President of India?

options.A: Citizen of India, completed 25 years of age, qualified for Lok Sabha membership
options.B: Citizen of India, completed 35 years of age, qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha, and not holding an office of profit
options.C: Citizen of India, completed 30 years of age, qualified for Rajya Sabha membership
options.D: Citizen of India, completed 40 years of age, qualified for Lok Sabha membership

questions.explanation: The person must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age, be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha, and not hold an office of profit under the Union, a State or a specified local or other authority, subject to constitutional exceptions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article prescribes the qualifications for election as President?
questions.explanation: Article 58 prescribes the qualifications for election as President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a sitting Governor or Union/State Minister contest the Presidential election merely because of holding that office?

options.A: No, holding such office disqualifies them
options.B: Yes, because the Constitution treats the offices of President, Vice-President, Governor and Minister as not being offices of profit for this purpose

questions.explanation: The Constitution treats the offices of President, Vice-President, Governor and Minister as not being offices of profit for this purpose; other disqualifications and eligibility conditions still apply.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the term of office of the President?

options.B: Five years from the date on which the President enters upon the office

questions.explanation: The President holds office for five years from the date on which the President enters upon the office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the President's term?
questions.explanation: Article 56 provides for the term of office of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President be re-elected?

options.B: Yes, Article 57 permits re-election with no limit on the number of terms
options.C: Yes, but only for one additional term
options.D: Only after a gap of five years

questions.explanation: Article 57 permits re-election; the Constitution sets no limit on the number of terms.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: To whom does the President submit a resignation?

options.C: The Vice-President, who communicates it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha directly

questions.explanation: The President submits resignation to the Vice-President, who communicates it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the President?

options.B: The Chief Justice of India; in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of India administers the oath; in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the President's oath?
questions.explanation: Article 60 provides for the oath or affirmation by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the minimum notice period for a resolution to impeach the President?

options.B: 14 days' written notice signed by not less than one-fourth of the total number of members of the House initiating the charge

questions.explanation: At least 14 days' written notice, signed by not less than one-fourth of the total number of members of the House initiating the charge, is required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: On what ground can the President be impeached?

options.A: Loss of majority in the Lok Sabha
options.B: Violation of the Constitution, under Article 61

questions.explanation: The President can be impeached for violation of the Constitution under Article 61.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can either House of Parliament initiate impeachment proceedings against the President?

options.A: No, only the Lok Sabha can
options.B: No, only the Rajya Sabha can
options.C: Yes, either House may prefer the charge; the other House investigates or causes the charge to be investigated
options.D: Only a joint sitting can initiate impeachment

questions.explanation: Either House may prefer the charge; the other House investigates or causes the charge to be investigated.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What majority is required to pass an impeachment resolution against the President?

options.A: Simple majority of members present and voting
options.B: A majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of each House, at the relevant stage
options.C: Three-fourths of the total membership of each House

questions.explanation: A majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of each House is required at the relevant stage.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can State Legislatures participate in the impeachment of the President?

options.B: No, impeachment is a parliamentary procedure involving the two Houses of Parliament

questions.explanation: Impeachment is a parliamentary procedure involving the two Houses of Parliament; State Legislatures do not participate.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who acts as President when the office falls vacant due to death, resignation, removal or otherwise?

options.C: The Vice-President, until a new President enters office, subject to Article 65
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Vice-President acts as President until a new President enters office, subject to Article 65.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Within what period must an election be held to fill a vacancy caused by the expiry of the President's term?

options.B: The election must be completed before the term expires

questions.explanation: The election must be completed before the term expires.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Within what period must an election be held to fill a casual vacancy in the office of President?

options.A: As soon as possible and in no case later than six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy

questions.explanation: The election must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy; the person elected serves a full five-year term from entering office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the major categories of the President's powers?

options.A: Executive, legislative, financial, judicial, diplomatic, military and emergency powers

questions.explanation: The President's powers include executive, legislative, financial, judicial, diplomatic, military and emergency powers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How are the Prime Minister and other Union Ministers appointed?

options.B: The President appoints the Prime Minister and, on the Prime Minister's advice, the other Ministers under Article 75
options.C: Appointed by the Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The President appoints the Prime Minister and, on the Prime Minister's advice, the other Ministers under Article 75.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the Attorney-General of India?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Attorney-General of India under Article 76.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the Governors of States?

options.A: The Chief Minister of the State

questions.explanation: The President appoints the Governors of States under Article 155.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under Article 148.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts?

options.B: The President formally appoints them under the relevant constitutional provisions, following the constitutionally established consultation and collegium process
options.C: The Chief Justice of India alone

questions.explanation: The President formally appoints the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts under the relevant constitutional provisions, following the constitutionally established consultation and collegium process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners?

options.B: The President, subject to the constitutional and statutory framework governing their appointment

questions.explanation: The President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, subject to the constitutional and statutory framework governing their appointment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the Chairperson and members of the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Chairperson and members of the Union Public Service Commission under Article 316.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the President's legislative role?

options.A: The President summons and prorogues Parliament, may dissolve the Lok Sabha, addresses Parliament, may send messages to Houses, gives assent to Bills, and may promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session and constitutional conditions are met
options.B: The President only gives assent to Bills
options.D: The President has no legislative role

questions.explanation: The President summons and prorogues Parliament, may dissolve the Lok Sabha, addresses Parliament, may send messages to Houses, gives assent to Bills, and may promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session and constitutional conditions are met.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with sessions, prorogation and dissolution of Parliament by the President?
questions.explanation: Article 85 deals with sessions, prorogation and dissolution of Parliament by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the President's special address to Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 87 provides for the President's special address to Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: When does the President address both Houses assembled together?

options.A: At the commencement of every session
options.B: At the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and at the commencement of the first session of each year

questions.explanation: The President addresses both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Lok Sabha and at the commencement of the first session of each year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President nominate members to the Rajya Sabha?

options.B: Yes, under Article 80 the President nominates 12 members having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service

questions.explanation: Under Article 80, the President nominates 12 members having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Does the President currently nominate Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha?

options.B: No, the former provision for nomination of up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha ceased under the 104th Constitutional Amendment

questions.explanation: The former provision for nomination of up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha ceased under the 104th Constitutional Amendment.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the President's ordinance-making power?

options.A: Under Article 123, the President may promulgate an Ordinance when both Houses of Parliament are not simultaneously in session and immediate action is necessary; it has the force of an Act but must be laid before Parliament and ordinarily ceases six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved
options.B: The President may promulgate Ordinances at any time, even when both Houses are in session
options.C: The President may promulgate Ordinances only during a National Emergency
options.D: The President has no ordinance-making power

questions.explanation: Under Article 123, the President may promulgate an Ordinance when both Houses of Parliament are not simultaneously in session and immediate action is necessary; the Ordinance has the force of an Act but must be laid before Parliament and ordinarily ceases six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved or otherwise dealt with.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can an Ordinance be promulgated when both Houses are in session?

options.B: No, because Article 123 requires that both Houses are not simultaneously in session
options.C: Yes, with the permission of the Speaker

questions.explanation: Article 123 requires that both Houses are not simultaneously in session for an Ordinance to be promulgated.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the maximum normal life of an Ordinance after Parliament reassembles, if not approved?

options.C: Six weeks after Parliament reassembles, subject to the constitutional calculation where the Houses reassemble on different dates

questions.explanation: An Ordinance ceases six weeks after Parliament reassembles, subject to the constitutional calculation where the Houses reassemble on different dates.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article gives the President power to grant pardons and other forms of clemency?
questions.explanation: Article 72 gives the President power to grant pardons and other forms of clemency.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What forms of clemency can the President grant under Article 72?

options.B: Pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, suspension or commutation of sentence in cases within the constitutional scope

questions.explanation: The President can grant pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, suspension or commutation of sentence in cases within the constitutional scope, including court-martial cases, offences under laws relating to matters within Union executive power, and all cases of death sentence.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President pardon a death sentence?

options.B: Yes, Article 72 expressly empowers the President to grant a pardon in all cases where a sentence of death has been passed
options.C: Only with the approval of Parliament
options.D: Only with the approval of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Article 72 expressly empowers the President to grant a pardon in all cases where a sentence of death has been passed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the President's financial role in relation to the Union Budget?

options.A: The Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses by the President under Article 112; certain financial proposals require the President's recommendation under the Constitution
options.B: The President votes on Demands for Grants
options.C: The President presents the Budget in the Lok Sabha
options.D: The President has no financial role

questions.explanation: The Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses by the President under Article 112; certain financial proposals require the President's recommendation under the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a Money Bill be introduced without the President's recommendation?

options.B: No, a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Lok Sabha except on the President's recommendation, under Article 117(1)

questions.explanation: A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Lok Sabha except on the President's recommendation, under Article 117(1).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the President's diplomatic role?

options.A: The President represents India in international affairs, appoints ambassadors and high commissioners, and receives foreign diplomatic representatives; these functions are exercised within the constitutional framework on ministerial advice
options.B: The President conducts all foreign negotiations personally
options.C: The President has no diplomatic role

questions.explanation: The President represents India in international affairs, appoints ambassadors and high commissioners, and receives foreign diplomatic representatives; these functions are exercised within the constitutional framework on ministerial advice.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the President's military role?

options.A: The President personally commands all military operations
options.B: The President is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces; the exercise of operational and policy functions is governed by the Constitution and laws and the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
options.C: The President has no military role
options.D: The President only appoints the Defence Minister

questions.explanation: The President is the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces; the exercise of operational and policy functions is governed by the Constitution and laws and the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with National Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 352 deals with National Emergency.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with President's Rule in a State?
questions.explanation: Article 356 deals with President's Rule in a State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with Financial Emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Is the President generally bound by the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers?

options.B: Yes, Article 74(1) requires the President to act in accordance with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister; the President may require the Council to reconsider its advice once, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after reconsideration

questions.explanation: Article 74(1) requires the President to act in accordance with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister; the President may require the Council to reconsider its advice once, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after reconsideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President ask the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice?

options.B: Yes, once under the proviso to Article 74(1)
options.D: Only with the approval of Parliament

questions.explanation: The President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice once under the proviso to Article 74(1).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a pocket veto?

options.A: A veto exercised by the Vice-President
options.B: The commonly used term for the President taking no action on a Bill for an indefinite period where the Constitution prescribes no specific time limit for assent or return; it is not expressly named in the Constitution
options.C: A veto by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: A pocket veto is the commonly used term for the President taking no action on a Bill for an indefinite period where the Constitution prescribes no specific time limit for assent or return; it is not expressly named in the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President return a Constitutional Amendment Bill for reconsideration?

options.B: No, under Article 368 the President shall give assent to a duly passed Constitutional Amendment Bill
options.C: Yes, if it violates fundamental rights
options.D: Only with the approval of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 368, the President shall give assent to a duly passed Constitutional Amendment Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President return an ordinary Bill for reconsideration?

options.B: Yes, the President may return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration; if Parliament passes it again, with or without amendment, the President shall not withhold assent

questions.explanation: The President may return a non-Money Bill once for reconsideration; if Parliament passes it again, with or without amendment, the President shall not withhold assent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President return a Money Bill for reconsideration?

options.B: No, Article 111's return power applies to Bills other than Money Bills

questions.explanation: Article 111's return power applies to Bills other than Money Bills; the President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the office of Vice-President of India?
questions.explanation: Article 63 provides for the office of Vice-President of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the principal ex-officio position held by the Vice-President?

options.B: Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64

questions.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How is the Vice-President elected?

options.A: By an electoral college consisting of all members of both Houses of Parliament, through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot
options.C: By the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
options.D: By a joint sitting of Parliament

questions.explanation: The Vice-President is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of all members of both Houses of Parliament, through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Are nominated members of Parliament eligible to vote in the Vice-Presidential election?

options.B: Yes, unlike the Presidential electoral college, the Vice-Presidential electoral college includes elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament

questions.explanation: Unlike the Presidential electoral college, the Vice-Presidential electoral college includes elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Do elected members of State Legislative Assemblies vote in the Vice-Presidential election?

options.D: Only the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

questions.explanation: Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies do not vote in the Vice-Presidential election.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the election of the Vice-President?
questions.explanation: Article 66 provides for the election of the Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the qualifications for election as Vice-President?

options.A: Citizen of India, completed 25 years of age, qualified for Lok Sabha membership
options.B: Citizen of India, completed 35 years of age, qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha, and not holding an office of profit
options.C: Citizen of India, completed 30 years of age, qualified for Rajya Sabha membership
options.D: Citizen of India, completed 40 years of age

questions.explanation: The person must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age, be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha, and not hold an office of profit under the Union, a State or a specified local or other authority, subject to constitutional exceptions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article prescribes the qualifications for Vice-President?
questions.explanation: Article 66(3) prescribes the qualifications for election as Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the term of office of the Vice-President?

options.B: Five years from the date on which the Vice-President enters office

questions.explanation: The Vice-President holds office for five years from the date on which the Vice-President enters office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with the term of the Vice-President?
questions.explanation: Article 67 deals with the term of office of the Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the Vice-President be re-elected?

options.B: Yes, the Constitution does not prescribe a limit on the number of terms
options.C: Yes, but only for one additional term
options.D: Only after a gap of five years

questions.explanation: The Vice-President can be re-elected; the Constitution does not prescribe a limit on the number of terms.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: To whom does the Vice-President submit a resignation?

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Vice-President submits resignation to the President of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How can the Vice-President be removed?

options.B: By a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha
options.C: By a resolution of the Lok Sabha only
options.D: By the President on the advice of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Is removal of the Vice-President called impeachment in the Constitution?

options.B: No, the Constitution uses a removal resolution procedure, not the impeachment procedure applicable to the President

questions.explanation: The Constitution uses a removal resolution procedure for the Vice-President, not the impeachment procedure applicable to the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What notice is required for a resolution to remove the Vice-President?

options.B: At least 14 days' notice must be given of the intention to move the resolution

questions.explanation: At least 14 days' notice must be given of the intention to move the resolution for removal of the Vice-President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who administers the oath to the Vice-President?

options.B: The President, or a person appointed by the President, under Article 69
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The President, or a person appointed by the President, administers the oath to the Vice-President under Article 69.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article allows the Vice-President to act as President?
questions.explanation: Article 65 allows the Vice-President to act as President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the Vice-President act as President while continuing to perform the duties of Rajya Sabha Chairman?

options.A: Yes, both duties can be performed simultaneously
options.B: No, while acting as President or discharging the President's functions, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha and is entitled to the President's emoluments and privileges for that period
options.C: Yes, with the permission of the Speaker

questions.explanation: While acting as President or discharging the President's functions, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha and is entitled to the President's emoluments and privileges for that period.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who presides over Rajya Sabha when the Vice-President is acting as President?

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person authorised under the rules

questions.explanation: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person authorised under the rules, presides over Rajya Sabha when the Vice-President is acting as President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who is the head of the Union Council of Ministers?

options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the head of the Union Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister?

options.B: The President of India under Article 75(1)

questions.explanation: The President of India appoints the Prime Minister under Article 75(1).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Whom does the President normally appoint as Prime Minister?

options.A: The leader who is able to command the confidence of the Lok Sabha, ordinarily the leader of the majority party or coalition
options.B: The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Any person recommended by the Chief Justice of India

questions.explanation: The President normally appoints as Prime Minister the leader who is able to command the confidence of the Lok Sabha, ordinarily the leader of the majority party or coalition.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Must the Prime Minister be a member of Parliament at the time of appointment?

options.B: The Constitution does not require membership at the moment of appointment, but the Prime Minister must become a member of either House of Parliament within six consecutive months or cease to be a Minister, under Article 75(5)
options.D: Only Lok Sabha membership is required

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not require membership at the moment of appointment, but the Prime Minister must become a member of either House of Parliament within six consecutive months or cease to be a Minister, under Article 75(5).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a member of the Rajya Sabha become Prime Minister?

options.A: No, only a Lok Sabha member can become Prime Minister
options.B: Yes, the Prime Minister may be a member of either House of Parliament
options.C: Yes, but only for six months
options.D: Only with the President's special permission

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister may be a member of either House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the constitutional tenure of the Prime Minister?

options.B: There is no fixed separate term; the Prime Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President and ordinarily continues while enjoying the confidence of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: There is no fixed separate term; the Prime Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President and ordinarily continues while enjoying the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the relationship between the Prime Minister and the President?

options.A: The Prime Minister is subordinate to the President in all matters
options.B: The Prime Minister is the principal channel of communication between the Council of Ministers and the President and performs the duties specified in Article 78
options.C: The Prime Minister has no constitutional relationship with the President
options.D: The Prime Minister only communicates on financial matters

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the principal channel of communication between the Council of Ministers and the President and performs the duties specified in Article 78.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the duties of the Prime Minister under Article 78?

options.A: To communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals; furnish information requested by the President; and submit for Council consideration a matter decided by an individual Minister if the President so requires
options.B: To preside over the Supreme Court
options.C: To appoint the Chief Election Commissioner

questions.explanation: Under Article 78, the Prime Minister communicates to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals; furnishes information requested by the President; and submits for Council consideration a matter decided by an individual Minister if the President so requires.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who allocates portfolios among Union Ministers?

options.B: The President appoints Ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister; in practice, the Prime Minister allocates and reshuffles portfolios within the constitutional framework

questions.explanation: The President appoints Ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister; in practice, the Prime Minister allocates and reshuffles portfolios within the constitutional framework.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who presides over meetings of the Union Cabinet?

options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister presides over meetings of the Union Cabinet.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who is the principal spokesperson and coordinator of the Union Government in Parliament?

options.B: The Prime Minister, supported by the Council of Ministers and parliamentary affairs machinery
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister, supported by the Council of Ministers and parliamentary affairs machinery, is the principal spokesperson and coordinator of the Union Government in Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens if the Prime Minister resigns?

options.A: Only the Prime Minister resigns; other Ministers continue
options.B: The Council of Ministers ordinarily resigns with the Prime Minister because it functions as a collective body headed by the Prime Minister
options.C: The President takes over the government
options.D: The Lok Sabha is automatically dissolved

questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers ordinarily resigns with the Prime Minister because it functions as a collective body headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens if the Prime Minister loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha?

options.A: The Prime Minister continues in office
options.B: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers must resign or seek dissolution in accordance with constitutional convention; the government cannot continue in office without Lok Sabha confidence
options.C: The President appoints a new Prime Minister without any process
options.D: The Rajya Sabha elects a new Prime Minister

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers must resign or seek dissolution in accordance with constitutional convention; the government cannot continue in office without Lok Sabha confidence.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President dismiss a Prime Minister who continues to enjoy the confidence of the Lok Sabha merely at personal discretion?

options.A: Yes, the President has absolute discretion
options.B: The President ordinarily acts on constitutional convention and ministerial advice; the Prime Minister's political authority depends on Lok Sabha confidence
options.C: Yes, with the approval of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: The President ordinarily acts on constitutional convention and ministerial advice; the Prime Minister's political authority depends on Lok Sabha confidence.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?

questions.question: Who is the Prime Minister of India as of 2 November 2026?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President?
questions.explanation: Article 74(1) provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who appoints the other Union Ministers?

options.B: The President appoints them on the advice of the Prime Minister under Article 75(1)

questions.explanation: The President appoints the other Union Ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister under Article 75(1).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: To whom is the Union Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
questions.explanation: The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What does collective responsibility mean?

options.A: Each Minister is responsible only for their own ministry
options.B: The Council of Ministers stands or falls together; it must retain the confidence of the Lok Sabha, and Ministers are collectively accountable for government decisions
options.C: The President is responsible for all government decisions
options.D: The Rajya Sabha supervises the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: Collective responsibility means the Council of Ministers stands or falls together; it must retain the confidence of the Lok Sabha, and Ministers are collectively accountable for government decisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is individual ministerial responsibility?

options.A: A Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President, which in practice is exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister; a Minister may be required to resign or be removed
options.B: A Minister is responsible only to the Rajya Sabha
options.C: A Minister cannot be removed once appointed
options.D: A Minister is responsible only to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Individual ministerial responsibility means a Minister holds office during the pleasure of the President, which in practice is exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister; a Minister may be required to resign or be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the maximum size of the Union Council of Ministers?

options.A: 10 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
options.B: 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha, under Article 75(1A)
options.C: 20 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
options.D: 25 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha, under Article 75(1A).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Amendment introduced the 15 per cent ceiling on the Union Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 introduced the 15 per cent ceiling on the Union Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the minimum size of the Union Council of Ministers under the Constitution?

options.C: The Constitution does not prescribe a general minimum number for the Union Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: The Constitution does not prescribe a general minimum number for the Union Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the maximum period a person who is not a member of Parliament may remain a Union Minister?

options.B: Six consecutive months; after that the person ceases to be a Minister unless becoming a member of either House of Parliament

questions.explanation: A person who is not a member of Parliament may remain a Union Minister for six consecutive months; after that the person ceases to be a Minister unless becoming a member of either House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who administers the oath of office and secrecy to Union Ministers?

options.B: The President under Article 75(4), according to the forms in the Third Schedule
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The President administers the oath of office and secrecy to Union Ministers under Article 75(4), according to the forms in the Third Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the main categories of Union Ministers by convention?

options.A: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (with independent charge or attached to a Cabinet Minister), and Ministers of State
options.B: Only Cabinet Ministers and Deputy Ministers
options.D: Senior Ministers and Junior Ministers only

questions.explanation: The main categories of Union Ministers by convention are Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State (with independent charge or attached to a Cabinet Minister), and Ministers of State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Is the term 'Cabinet' defined in the Constitution?

options.A: No, the term is not found in the Constitution
options.B: Yes, Article 352(3) defines the Union Cabinet for the purpose of a written decision authorising a National Emergency proclamation; the Constitution does not comprehensively enumerate every aspect of Cabinet composition
options.C: Yes, Article 74 defines the Cabinet in detail
options.D: Yes, Article 75 defines the Cabinet in detail

questions.explanation: Article 352(3) defines the Union Cabinet for the purpose of a written decision authorising a National Emergency proclamation; the Constitution does not comprehensively enumerate every aspect of Cabinet composition.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the difference between the Council of Ministers and the Cabinet?

options.B: The Council of Ministers is the larger constitutional body of all Ministers; the Cabinet is the smaller senior decision-making body consisting of Cabinet Ministers and certain invited members as per government practice
options.C: The Cabinet is larger than the Council of Ministers
options.D: The Council of Ministers is a committee of the Cabinet

questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is the larger constitutional body of all Ministers; the Cabinet is the smaller senior decision-making body consisting of Cabinet Ministers and certain invited members as per government practice.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with the conduct of business of the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Article 77 deals with the conduct of business of the Government of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who communicates Council of Ministers' decisions and legislative proposals to the President?

options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Prime Minister communicates Council of Ministers' decisions and legislative proposals to the President under Article 78.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Parliament of India?
questions.explanation: Article 79 provides for the Parliament of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the components of the Parliament of India?

options.A: The President, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Prime Minister, the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha only
options.D: The President and the Lok Sabha only

questions.explanation: The Parliament of India consists of the President, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Is the President a member of either House of Parliament?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?

questions.question: How many members may the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the constitutional maximum strength of the Lok Sabha under Article 81 after the 104th Amendment?

options.B: 550 members: up to 530 members representing States and up to 20 members representing Union Territories

questions.explanation: After the 104th Amendment, the House may consist of up to 530 members representing States and up to 20 members representing Union Territories; the former provision for nominated Anglo-Indian members ceased.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the normal duration of the Lok Sabha?

options.B: Five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved

questions.explanation: The Lok Sabha's normal duration is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved; during a National Emergency, Parliament may extend its term by law for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for the duration of the Houses of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 83 provides for the duration of the Houses of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Is the Rajya Sabha a permanent House?

options.A: No, it is dissolved every five years
options.B: Yes, it is not subject to dissolution
options.C: Yes, but it is dissolved during a National Emergency
options.D: No, it is dissolved with the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House; it is not subject to dissolution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What fraction of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years?

options.B: As nearly as possible, one-third of its members retire every second year

questions.explanation: As nearly as possible, one-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every second year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the normal term of a Rajya Sabha member?
questions.explanation: The normal term of a Rajya Sabha member is six years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who determines the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to States and Union Territories?

options.B: The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution, subject to constitutional and statutory provisions

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article deals with voting in Houses, vacancies and quorum?
questions.explanation: Article 100 deals with voting in Houses, vacancies and quorum.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament?

options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then such other person as determined under the constitutional and procedural rules
options.D: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then such other person as determined under the constitutional and procedural rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article provides for a joint sitting of both Houses?
questions.explanation: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of both Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: When can a joint sitting be called?

options.A: For resolving a deadlock on an ordinary Bill when one House rejects it, the Houses finally disagree on amendments, or more than six months elapse without passage by the other House, subject to constitutional exclusions
options.B: For any Bill at any time

questions.explanation: A joint sitting can be called for resolving a deadlock on an ordinary Bill when one House rejects it, the Houses finally disagree on amendments, or more than six months elapse without passage by the other House, subject to constitutional exclusions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a joint sitting be called for a Money Bill?

questions.explanation: A joint sitting cannot be called for a Money Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a joint sitting be called for a Constitutional Amendment Bill?

options.B: No, a Constitutional Amendment Bill must be passed separately by each House with the required majority
options.C: Only if the Rajya Sabha rejects it
options.D: Only if the Supreme Court permits

questions.explanation: A joint sitting cannot be called for a Constitutional Amendment Bill; it must be passed separately by each House with the required majority.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who summons each House of Parliament?

options.D: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is prorogation?

options.A: The suspension of a sitting of a House for a specified time
options.B: The formal termination of a session of a House by the President
options.C: The formal end of the Lok Sabha's life
options.D: The termination of a sitting without fixing a date for the next sitting

questions.explanation: Prorogation is the formal termination of a session of a House by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is adjournment?

options.A: The formal termination of a session by the President
options.B: The suspension of a sitting of a House for a specified time by the presiding officer; it does not terminate the session
options.C: The formal end of the Lok Sabha's life
options.D: The termination of a sitting without fixing a date for the next sitting

questions.explanation: Adjournment is the suspension of a sitting of a House for a specified time by the presiding officer; it does not terminate the session.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is adjournment sine die?

options.A: The formal termination of a session by the President
options.B: The termination of a sitting of a House without fixing a date for its next sitting; the session may later be prorogued by the President
options.C: The dissolution of the Lok Sabha
options.D: The suspension of a sitting for a specified time

questions.explanation: Adjournment sine die is the termination of a sitting of a House without fixing a date for its next sitting; the session may later be prorogued by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is dissolution?

options.A: The formal termination of a session of a House
options.B: The formal end of the Lok Sabha's life; it does not apply to the Rajya Sabha
options.C: The suspension of a sitting for a specified time
options.D: The termination of a sitting without fixing a date for the next sitting

questions.explanation: Dissolution is the formal end of the Lok Sabha's life; it does not apply to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens to a Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?

questions.question: What happens to a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?

questions.question: What happens to a Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration

questions.question: What is Zero Hour?

options.D: The period for voting on Demands for Grants

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a starred question?

options.B: A question for which an oral answer is sought and supplementary questions may be asked

options.D: A question asked by a Minister

questions.explanation: A starred question is a question for which an oral answer is sought and supplementary questions may be asked.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is an unstarred question?

options.A: A question for which an oral answer is sought
options.B: A question answered in writing; supplementary questions are not permitted
options.C: A question asked with shorter notice
options.D: A question asked by a Minister

questions.explanation: An unstarred question is a question answered in writing; supplementary questions are not permitted.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a short-notice question?

options.B: A question on a matter of urgent public importance asked with shorter notice than ordinarily prescribed, subject to the presiding officer's permission
options.C: A question asked by a Minister
options.D: A question asked during Zero Hour

questions.explanation: A short-notice question is a question on a matter of urgent public importance asked with shorter notice than ordinarily prescribed, subject to the presiding officer's permission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a no-confidence motion?

options.B: A motion moved in the Lok Sabha to test whether the Council of Ministers continues to enjoy the confidence of the House
options.C: A motion to reduce a Demand for Grant
options.D: A motion expressing disapproval of a policy

questions.explanation: A no-confidence motion is a motion moved in the Lok Sabha to test whether the Council of Ministers continues to enjoy the confidence of the House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a no-confidence motion be moved in the Rajya Sabha to remove the Union Council of Ministers?

questions.explanation: A no-confidence motion cannot be moved in the Rajya Sabha; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a censure motion?

options.A: A motion to remove the Council of Ministers
options.B: A motion expressing disapproval of a specified policy, action or conduct of the government or a Minister; it differs from a no-confidence motion
options.C: A motion to reduce a Demand for Grant
options.D: A motion to adjourn the House

questions.explanation: A censure motion is a motion expressing disapproval of a specified policy, action or conduct of the government or a Minister; it differs from a no-confidence motion.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a cut motion?

options.A: A motion moved during discussion of Demands for Grants to reduce a demand, used as a parliamentary instrument of financial control

questions.question: Who elects the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
