questions.explanation: Article 80 provides for the composition of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Is the Rajya Sabha a permanent House?

options.A: No, it is dissolved every five years
options.C: Yes, but it is dissolved during a National Emergency
options.D: No, it is dissolved with the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House; it is never dissolved.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The minimum age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How are elected Rajya Sabha members chosen?

options.B: They are elected by elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, using proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote; the constitutional and statutory arrangements also cover eligible Union Territories

questions.explanation: Elected Rajya Sabha members are chosen by elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, using proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote; the constitutional and statutory arrangements also cover eligible Union Territories.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha?

options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The President of India nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the term of a Rajya Sabha member?

options.C: Six years, with approximately one-third retiring every two years

questions.explanation: The term of a Rajya Sabha member is six years, with approximately one-third retiring every two years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?

options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who elects the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?

options.B: The Rajya Sabha elects the Deputy Chairman from among its members under Article 89(2)

questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha elects the Deputy Chairman from among its members under Article 89(2).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha vote in the first instance?

options.B: No, the Chairman does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in case of equality of votes

questions.explanation: The Chairman does not vote in the first instance but has a casting vote in case of equality of votes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What special powers does Rajya Sabha have under Article 249?

options.A: It may pass a resolution, supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting, declaring it necessary in the national interest for Parliament to make laws on a matter in the State List
options.B: It may remove the Council of Ministers
options.C: It may amend the Constitution alone
options.D: It may approve a National Emergency

questions.explanation: Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha may pass a resolution, supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting, declaring it necessary in the national interest for Parliament to make laws on a matter in the State List.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the duration of a resolution under Article 249?

options.B: It remains in force for a period not exceeding one year and may be renewed for further periods not exceeding one year at a time; laws made under it cease to have effect six months after the resolution ceases, subject to the constitutional provision

questions.explanation: A resolution under Article 249 remains in force for a period not exceeding one year and may be renewed for further periods not exceeding one year at a time; laws made under it cease to have effect six months after the resolution ceases, subject to the constitutional provision.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What special power does Rajya Sabha have under Article 312?

options.A: It may authorise Parliament to create one or more All India Services common to the Union and States, by a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting
options.D: It may dissolve the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 312, the Rajya Sabha may authorise Parliament to create one or more All India Services common to the Union and States, by a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can Rajya Sabha reject or amend a Money Bill?

options.A: Yes, it can reject or amend a Money Bill
options.B: It cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it may only recommend amendments and must return it within 14 days
options.C: It can amend a Money Bill with the Speaker's permission
options.D: It can reject a Money Bill but not amend it

questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it may only recommend amendments and must return it within 14 days.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can Rajya Sabha pass a no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha cannot pass a no-confidence motion against the Union Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can Rajya Sabha participate in impeachment of the President?

options.A: No, only the Lok Sabha can
options.B: Yes, both Houses participate in the impeachment process under Article 61
options.C: Only if the Lok Sabha requests

questions.explanation: Both Houses participate in the impeachment of the President under Article 61.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Parliamentary Committee?

options.A: A committee appointed or elected by a House, or nominated by the Speaker or Chairman, which works under the direction of the presiding officer and presents a report to the House or presiding officer
options.B: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.C: A committee of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: A Parliamentary Committee is a committee appointed or elected by a House, or nominated by the Speaker or Chairman, which works under the direction of the presiding officer and presents a report to the House or presiding officer.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Why are Parliamentary Committees necessary?

options.A: They enable detailed examination of complex issues, improve legislative scrutiny, monitor expenditure and strengthen executive accountability when plenary House time is limited
options.B: They replace the Houses of Parliament
options.C: They make binding decisions on the Government
options.D: They are required by the Constitution for every Bill

questions.explanation: Parliamentary Committees enable detailed examination of complex issues, improve legislative scrutiny, monitor expenditure and strengthen executive accountability when plenary House time is limited.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the two broad categories of Parliamentary Committees?

options.A: Standing Committees and Ad hoc Committees
options.C: Lok Sabha Committees and Rajya Sabha Committees

questions.explanation: The two broad categories of Parliamentary Committees are Standing Committees and Ad hoc Committees.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Standing Committee?

options.A: A committee constituted for a specific purpose
options.B: A committee constituted on a continuing basis under parliamentary rules, usually reconstituted periodically, to perform specified functions
options.C: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.D: A committee of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: A Standing Committee is a committee constituted on a continuing basis under parliamentary rules, usually reconstituted periodically, to perform specified functions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is an Ad hoc Committee?

options.A: A committee constituted on a continuing basis
options.B: A committee constituted for a specific purpose; it ceases to exist after submitting its report or completing the assigned task
options.C: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.D: A committee of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: An Ad hoc Committee is a committee constituted for a specific purpose; it ceases to exist after submitting its report or completing the assigned task.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are the three principal financial committees of Parliament?

options.A: The Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee, Business Advisory Committee and Rules Committee
options.C: The Estimates Committee, Ethics Committee and Privileges Committee
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee, Petitions Committee and Government Assurances Committee

questions.explanation: The three principal financial committees of Parliament are the Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How many members are in the Public Accounts Committee?

options.A: 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.D: 15 members, all from the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the normal tenure of the Public Accounts Committee?
questions.explanation: The normal tenure of the Public Accounts Committee is one year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who chairs the Public Accounts Committee by convention?

options.A: A member of the ruling party
options.B: A member of the Opposition is conventionally appointed Chairperson; this is a parliamentary convention, not a constitutional requirement
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: A member of the Opposition is conventionally appointed Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee; this is a parliamentary convention, not a constitutional requirement.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the principal function of the Public Accounts Committee?

options.A: To examine the appropriation accounts and finance accounts of the Union and reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General, and assess whether public money was legally and properly spent
options.B: To examine the estimates and suggest economies
options.C: To examine the reports of public undertakings
options.D: To examine Bills referred to it

questions.explanation: The principal function of the Public Accounts Committee is to examine the appropriation accounts and finance accounts of the Union and reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General, and assess whether public money was legally and properly spent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How many members are in the Estimates Committee?

options.A: 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.D: 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can Rajya Sabha members serve on the Estimates Committee?

options.B: No, it is a Lok Sabha committee

questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha members cannot serve on the Estimates Committee; it is a Lok Sabha committee.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the principal function of the Estimates Committee?

options.A: To examine estimates, suggest economies and improvements in organisation and administration, and recommend greater efficiency in public expenditure
options.C: To examine the reports of public undertakings
options.D: To examine Bills referred to it

questions.explanation: The principal function of the Estimates Committee is to examine estimates, suggest economies and improvements in organisation and administration, and recommend greater efficiency in public expenditure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How many members are in the Committee on Public Undertakings?

options.A: 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.C: 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the principal function of the Committee on Public Undertakings?

options.A: To examine reports and accounts of specified public undertakings and reports of the CAG relating to them, and assess whether they are managed efficiently and in accordance with sound business principles
options.C: To examine estimates and suggest economies
options.D: To examine Bills referred to it

questions.explanation: The principal function of the Committee on Public Undertakings is to examine reports and accounts of specified public undertakings and reports of the CAG relating to them, and assess whether they are managed efficiently and in accordance with sound business principles.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What are Department-related Standing Committees (DRSCs)?

options.A: Committees that examine the Demands for Grants of ministries and departments, Bills referred to them, annual reports and long-term policy documents within their assigned jurisdiction
options.B: Committees that examine the appropriation accounts
options.C: Committees that examine breach of privilege

questions.explanation: Department-related Standing Committees examine the Demands for Grants of ministries and departments, Bills referred to them, annual reports and long-term policy documents within their assigned jurisdiction.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How many Department-related Standing Committees are there at present?
questions.explanation: There are 24 Department-related Standing Committees at present.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: How many members are in each DRSC?

options.A: 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.C: 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Each DRSC has 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the normal tenure of a DRSC?
questions.explanation: The normal tenure of a DRSC is not more than one year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: When were Department-related Standing Committees introduced in Parliament?

options.A: They were introduced in 1993, initially as 17 committees; the system was expanded to 24 in 2004

questions.explanation: Department-related Standing Committees were introduced in 1993, initially as 17 committees; the system was expanded to 24 in 2004.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a Minister be a member of a Department-related Standing Committee?

options.B: No, Ministers are not eligible for membership of these committees

questions.explanation: Ministers are not eligible for membership of Department-related Standing Committees.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Select Committee on a Bill?

options.A: A committee of members of one House appointed to examine a particular Bill and report to that House
options.B: A committee of members from both Houses
options.C: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.D: A committee of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: A Select Committee on a Bill is a committee of members of one House appointed to examine a particular Bill and report to that House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Joint Committee on a Bill?

options.A: A committee of members of one House
options.B: A committee consisting of members from both Houses, constituted to examine a particular Bill and report to Parliament
options.C: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.D: A committee of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: A Joint Committee on a Bill consists of members from both Houses, constituted to examine a particular Bill and report to Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)?

options.A: A committee of members from both Houses constituted by Parliament to investigate or examine a specified matter, often on a motion adopted by the Houses
options.B: A committee of the Supreme Court
options.C: A committee of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: A Joint Parliamentary Committee is a committee of members from both Houses constituted by Parliament to investigate or examine a specified matter, often on a motion adopted by the Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Committee on Petitions?

options.A: A committee that examines petitions presented to the House and reports on matters referred to it
options.B: A committee that examines breach of privilege
options.C: A committee that examines government assurances
options.D: A committee that recommends allocation of time

questions.explanation: The Committee on Petitions examines petitions presented to the House and reports on matters referred to it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Committee of Privileges?

options.A: A committee that examines questions involving breach of privilege or contempt and recommends action to the House
options.C: A committee that examines government assurances
options.D: A committee that recommends allocation of time

questions.explanation: The Committee of Privileges examines questions involving breach of privilege or contempt and recommends action to the House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Committee on Government Assurances?

options.A: A committee that scrutinises assurances, promises and undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House and examines their implementation
options.C: A committee that examines breach of privilege
options.D: A committee that recommends allocation of time

questions.explanation: The Committee on Government Assurances scrutinises assurances, promises and undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House and examines their implementation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Business Advisory Committee?

options.A: A committee that recommends allocation of time for government and other business in the House
options.C: A committee that examines breach of privilege
options.D: A committee that examines government assurances

questions.explanation: The Business Advisory Committee recommends allocation of time for government and other business in the House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Rules Committee?

options.A: A committee that considers matters relating to the rules of procedure and conduct of business of the House
options.C: A committee that examines breach of privilege
options.D: A committee that examines government assurances

questions.explanation: The Rules Committee considers matters relating to the rules of procedure and conduct of business of the House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Ethics Committee?

options.A: A committee that examines complaints or matters concerning ethical conduct of members under the relevant House rules
options.C: A committee that examines breach of privilege
options.D: A committee that examines government assurances

questions.explanation: The Ethics Committee examines complaints or matters concerning ethical conduct of members under the relevant House rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Are Parliamentary Committee reports binding on the Government?

options.B: Generally no; they are recommendatory, but they carry parliamentary significance and the Government may be expected to respond
options.C: Yes, if approved by the Speaker
options.D: Yes, if approved by the President

questions.explanation: Parliamentary Committee reports are generally not binding on the Government; they are recommendatory, but they carry parliamentary significance and the Government may be expected to respond.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Bill?

options.A: A draft legislative proposal presented to Parliament for consideration and approval; after being passed as required and receiving the President's assent, it becomes an Act
options.C: A rule made by the executive
options.D: A judgment of the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: A Bill is a draft legislative proposal presented to Parliament for consideration and approval; after being passed as required and receiving the President's assent, it becomes an Act.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Government Bill?

options.A: A Bill introduced by a Minister on behalf of the Government
options.B: A Bill introduced by a private member
options.C: A Bill introduced by the President
options.D: A Bill introduced by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: A Government Bill is a Bill introduced by a Minister on behalf of the Government.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Private Member's Bill?

options.A: A Bill introduced by a Minister
options.B: A Bill introduced by a member of Parliament who is not a Minister
options.C: A Bill introduced by the President
options.D: A Bill introduced by a State Legislature

questions.explanation: A Private Member's Bill is a Bill introduced by a member of Parliament who is not a Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is an Ordinary Bill?

options.A: A Bill dealing with matters other than those classified as Money Bills or specified Financial Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills
options.B: A Bill dealing only with taxation
options.C: A Bill dealing only with constitutional amendments
options.D: A Bill dealing only with expenditure from the Consolidated Fund

questions.explanation: An Ordinary Bill deals with matters other than those classified as Money Bills or specified Financial Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: In which House can an Ordinary Bill be introduced?

options.C: In either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: An Ordinary Bill can be introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Money Bill?

options.A: A Bill containing only provisions dealing with one or more matters listed in Article 110(1), such as taxation, government borrowing, custody or appropriation of the Consolidated Fund of India, charged expenditure, and related incidental matters
options.C: A Bill dealing only with constitutional amendments
options.D: A Bill introduced by a private member

questions.explanation: A Money Bill contains only provisions dealing with one or more matters listed in Article 110(1), such as taxation, government borrowing, custody or appropriation of the Consolidated Fund of India, charged expenditure, and related incidental matters.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article defines a Money Bill?
questions.explanation: Article 110 defines a Money Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Who certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill?

options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha; the Speaker's decision is final under Article 110(3), and the certificate is endorsed when the Bill is transmitted or presented
options.D: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill; the Speaker's decision is final under Article 110(3), and the certificate is endorsed when the Bill is transmitted or presented.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Where can a Money Bill be introduced?

options.B: Only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the President's recommendation

questions.explanation: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the President's recommendation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can Rajya Sabha amend a Money Bill?

options.A: Yes, it can amend a Money Bill
options.B: No, it can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject

questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha cannot amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Within how many days must Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days of receiving it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens if Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days?

options.B: The Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Bill is sent to a joint sitting
options.D: The Bill is referred to the President

questions.explanation: If Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President return a Money Bill for reconsideration?
questions.explanation: The President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Financial Bill under Article 117?

options.A: A Bill dealing with financial matters that does not necessarily meet the narrow definition of a Money Bill under Article 110; the Constitution distinguishes Financial Bills under Article 117(1) and Article 117(3)
options.B: A Bill that is always a Money Bill
options.C: A Bill dealing only with constitutional amendments
options.D: A Bill introduced by a private member

questions.explanation: A Financial Bill under Article 117 deals with financial matters that do not necessarily meet the narrow definition of a Money Bill under Article 110; the Constitution distinguishes Financial Bills under Article 117(1) and Article 117(3).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Financial Bill under Article 117(1)?

options.A: A Bill containing one or more matters specified in Article 110(1) along with other matters; it can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation, but Rajya Sabha has ordinary legislative powers over it, subject to the relevant provisions
options.B: A Bill that can be introduced in either House without the President's recommendation
options.C: A Bill dealing only with constitutional amendments
options.D: A Bill introduced by a private member

questions.explanation: A Financial Bill under Article 117(1) contains one or more matters specified in Article 110(1) along with other matters; it can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation, but Rajya Sabha has ordinary legislative powers over it, subject to the relevant provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Financial Bill under Article 117(3)?

options.A: A Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India; it may be introduced in either House but cannot be passed unless the President has recommended its consideration
options.B: A Bill that can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha
options.C: A Bill dealing only with taxation
options.D: A Bill that is always a Money Bill

questions.explanation: A Financial Bill under Article 117(3) is a Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India; it may be introduced in either House but cannot be passed unless the President has recommended its consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is a Constitutional Amendment Bill?

options.A: A Bill introduced to amend the Constitution under Article 368; it must be passed separately by each House with the constitutionally prescribed majority, and specified federal amendments also require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures
options.B: A Bill that can be passed by a simple majority
options.C: A Bill that can be introduced in a State Legislature
options.D: A Bill that can be returned by the President

questions.explanation: A Constitutional Amendment Bill is introduced to amend the Constitution under Article 368; it must be passed separately by each House with the constitutionally prescribed majority, and specified federal amendments also require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a Constitutional Amendment Bill be introduced in a State Legislature?

options.B: No, it can be introduced only in either House of Parliament
options.C: Only in the State Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: A Constitutional Amendment Bill can be introduced only in either House of Parliament, not in a State Legislature.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can the President return a Constitutional Amendment Bill?

options.B: No, the President must give assent after it is duly passed under Article 368
options.C: Yes, if it violates fundamental rights
options.D: Only with the Supreme Court's approval

questions.explanation: The President must give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill after it is duly passed under Article 368; the President cannot return it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the First Reading of a Bill?

options.A: The introduction of the Bill in the House, usually after leave to introduce is granted; a Bill passed by the other House is laid before the receiving House
options.B: The clause-by-clause consideration of the Bill
options.C: The final vote on the Bill
options.D: The President's assent to the Bill

questions.explanation: The First Reading of a Bill is the introduction of the Bill in the House, usually after leave to introduce is granted; a Bill passed by the other House is laid before the receiving House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens during the Second Reading?

options.A: The House considers the general principles and provisions, may refer the Bill to a Select or Joint Committee or circulate it for public opinion, and then undertakes clause-by-clause consideration and consideration of amendments
options.B: The Bill is introduced in the House
options.C: The Bill is sent to the President
options.D: The Bill is voted upon finally

questions.explanation: During the Second Reading, the House considers the general principles and provisions, may refer the Bill to a Select or Joint Committee or circulate it for public opinion, and then undertakes clause-by-clause consideration and consideration of amendments.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the Third Reading?

options.B: The final stage at which the House debates whether the Bill, in its final form, should be passed and then votes on it

questions.explanation: The Third Reading is the final stage at which the House debates whether the Bill, in its final form, should be passed and then votes on it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens after a Bill is passed by the House where it originated?

options.A: It is sent directly to the President
options.B: It is transmitted to the other House, where it ordinarily goes through the relevant stages of consideration and passage
options.D: It is sent to a joint sitting

questions.explanation: After a Bill is passed by the House where it originated, it is transmitted to the other House, where it ordinarily goes through the relevant stages of consideration and passage.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens after both Houses pass an ordinary Bill in the same form?

options.A: The Bill becomes an Act immediately
options.B: The Bill is presented to the President for assent
options.C: The Bill is sent to a joint sitting
options.D: The Bill is sent to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: After both Houses pass an ordinary Bill in the same form, the Bill is presented to the President for assent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What options does the President have on an ordinary Bill under Article 111?

options.A: The President may assent, withhold assent, or return a Bill other than a Money Bill for reconsideration; if Parliament passes it again, the President shall not withhold assent
options.C: The President may only withhold assent
options.D: The President may only return the Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 111, the President may assent, withhold assent, or return a Bill other than a Money Bill for reconsideration; if Parliament passes it again, the President shall not withhold assent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What happens if the two Houses disagree on an Ordinary Bill?

options.B: The President may summon a joint sitting under Article 108, subject to the constitutional conditions and exceptions
options.C: The Lok Sabha's version automatically prevails
options.D: The Rajya Sabha's version automatically prevails

questions.explanation: If the two Houses disagree on an Ordinary Bill, the President may summon a joint sitting under Article 108, subject to the constitutional conditions and exceptions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Can a joint sitting resolve a deadlock on a Constitutional Amendment Bill?

options.D: Only if the Supreme Court permits

questions.explanation: A joint sitting cannot resolve a deadlock on a Constitutional Amendment Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is the role of a Parliamentary Committee in the law-making process?

options.A: It may examine the Bill clause by clause, hear stakeholders or experts where appropriate, and submit recommendations to the House; the House retains the final decision
options.C: It gives assent to the Bill
options.D: It can reject the Bill permanently

questions.explanation: A Parliamentary Committee may examine the Bill clause by clause, hear stakeholders or experts where appropriate, and submit recommendations to the House; the House retains the final decision.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: What is an Ordinance?

options.A: A temporary law promulgated by the President under Article 123 when both Houses are not simultaneously in session and immediate action is necessary; it has the same force as an Act while in operation, subject to constitutional limits
options.B: A permanent law passed by Parliament

questions.question: What is a Token Cut Motion?

questions.question: Which Article provides for the oath or affirmation by the President?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, if a charge of violation of the Constitution is preferred against the President by one House, what must the other House do?

options.C: It must refer the matter to the Supreme Court

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(1), the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice. How many times may the President do so?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(1), after the Council of Ministers reconsiders its advice, the President must act in accordance with which advice?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 85, what is the maximum gap permitted between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Under Article 85, six months may not intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next session.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 87, the President addresses both Houses assembled together at which of the following occasions?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108, a joint sitting may be summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock on an ordinary Bill in which of the following situations?

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 111, if the President returns a non-Money Bill for reconsideration and Parliament passes it again, with or without amendment, what must the President do?

options.B: The President shall not withhold assent
options.C: The President may refer it to the Supreme Court
options.D: The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 111, if Parliament passes the Bill again, with or without amendment, the President shall not withhold assent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: The emoluments and allowances of the President
options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), the emoluments and allowances of the President are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: The salaries and allowances of the presiding officers of Parliament
options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), the salaries and allowances of the presiding officers of Parliament are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Debt charges for which the Government of India is liable
options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), debt charges for which the Government of India is liable are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: The salaries and pensions of Supreme Court judges
options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), the salaries and pensions of Supreme Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), which of the following is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), CAG-related expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 114, amendments to an Appropriation Bill cannot be moved in a manner that does what?

options.A: Varies the amount or alters the destination of a grant or charged expenditure

questions.explanation: Under Article 114, amendments to an Appropriation Bill cannot be moved in a manner that would vary the amount or alter the destination of a grant or charged expenditure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116, a Vote on Account is granted for what purpose?

options.A: To enable the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the full Budget process
options.B: To meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character
options.C: To meet a special purpose forming no part of the current service
options.D: To meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116, a Vote on Account is granted to enable the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the full Budget process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116, a Vote of Credit is granted for what purpose?

options.A: To enable the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year
options.B: To meet an unexpected demand of such magnitude or indefinite character that it cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Budget
options.C: To meet a special purpose forming no part of the current service
options.D: To meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116, a Vote of Credit is granted to meet an unexpected demand of such magnitude or indefinite character that it cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Budget.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116, an Exceptional Grant is granted for what purpose?

options.A: To enable the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year
options.B: To meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character
options.C: For a special purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year
options.D: To meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116, an Exceptional Grant is granted for a special purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115, a Supplementary Grant is sought when which of the following situations arises?

options.A: When the amount authorised for a service in the current financial year is insufficient
options.B: When a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement is required
options.C: When more money has been spent on a service than was authorised for that year
options.D: When an unforeseen expenditure needs to be met pending parliamentary authorisation

questions.explanation: Under Article 115, a Supplementary Grant is sought when the amount authorised for a service in the current financial year is insufficient.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115, an Additional Grant is sought when which of the following situations arises?

options.A: When the amount authorised for a service in the current financial year is insufficient
options.B: When a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement for that year is required
options.C: When more money has been spent on a service than was authorised for that year
options.D: When an unforeseen expenditure needs to be met pending parliamentary authorisation

questions.explanation: Under Article 115, an Additional Grant is sought when a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement for that year is required.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115, an Excess Grant is sought when which of the following situations arises?

options.A: When the amount authorised for a service in the current financial year is insufficient
options.B: When a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement is required
options.C: When more money has been spent on a service than was authorised for that year; it is presented after the expenditure has occurred and requires parliamentary regularisation
options.D: When an unforeseen expenditure needs to be met pending parliamentary authorisation

questions.explanation: Under Article 115, an Excess Grant is sought when more money has been spent on a service than was authorised for that year; it is presented after the expenditure has occurred and requires parliamentary regularisation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 267, the Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 267, the Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 266(2), the Public Account of India includes money received by or on behalf of the Government other than which of the following?

options.A: Revenues and public loans credited to the Consolidated Fund of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 266(2), the Public Account of India includes money received by or on behalf of the Government other than revenues and public loans credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no member of Parliament is liable to proceedings in any court in respect of which of the following?

options.A: Anything said or any vote given in Parliament or a committee thereof
options.B: Any criminal act committed outside Parliament
options.D: Any act done before becoming a member

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), no member of Parliament is liable to proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given in Parliament or a committee thereof.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no person is liable to proceedings in any court in respect of publication by or under the authority of either House of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), no person is liable to proceedings in any court in respect of publication by or under the authority of either House of reports, papers, votes or proceedings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 361A, protection is provided for publication of substantially true reports of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 361A, protection is provided for publication of substantially true reports of parliamentary and State Legislature proceedings, subject to its conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of the President and two Houses, namely the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 80, how many members may the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80, the President nominates twelve members to the Rajya Sabha having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 81, the Lok Sabha consists of members directly elected by the people from territorial constituencies on the basis of what?
questions.explanation: Under Article 81, the Lok Sabha consists of members directly elected by the people from territorial constituencies on the basis of adult suffrage.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 84, what is the minimum age for a person to be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84, the minimum age for a person to be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 84, what is the minimum age for a person to be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84, the minimum age for a person to be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha elects which of the following from among its members?

options.C: The Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister

questions.explanation: Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha elects the Speaker and Deputy Speaker from among its members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 89(2), the Rajya Sabha elects which of the following from among its members?
questions.explanation: Under Article 89(2), the Rajya Sabha elects the Deputy Chairman from among its members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 94, the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution of the Lok Sabha and continues until when?

options.A: Immediately before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha
options.C: The President appoints a new Speaker
options.D: The next general election is announced

questions.explanation: Under Article 94, the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution of the Lok Sabha and continues until immediately before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 94, the Speaker may be removed from office by a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by what majority?

options.A: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.B: A majority of all the then members of the House
options.C: A two-thirds majority of the total membership
options.D: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 94, the Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 94, what notice period is required for a resolution to remove the Speaker?
questions.explanation: Under Article 94, at least 14 days' notice is required for a resolution to remove the Speaker.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 89(1), the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of which body?
questions.explanation: Under Article 89(1), the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 89(2), the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is elected by whom?

options.B: The Rajya Sabha from among its members

questions.explanation: Under Article 89(2), the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is elected by the Rajya Sabha from among its members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 90, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by what majority?

options.A: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.B: A majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha
options.C: A two-thirds majority of the total membership
options.D: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 90, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(1), all questions at any sitting of either House or a joint sitting of the two Houses shall be determined by what majority?

options.A: A majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or Chairman
options.B: A two-thirds majority of the total membership
options.C: A simple majority of the total membership
options.D: A three-fourths majority of the members present and voting

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(1), all questions at any sitting of either House or a joint sitting of the two Houses shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or Chairman.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(1), the Speaker or Chairman of a House shall have a casting vote in which situation?

options.B: When the House is deciding on a Money Bill
options.C: When the House is deciding on a no-confidence motion
options.D: When the House is deciding on a Constitutional Amendment Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(1), the Speaker or Chairman shall have a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 121, no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of which of the following?

options.A: Any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties
options.B: The President in the discharge of his duties
options.C: The Prime Minister in the discharge of his duties
options.D: The Speaker in the discharge of his duties

questions.explanation: Under Article 121, no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 122, the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on which ground?

options.A: On the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure
options.B: On the ground of violation of the Constitution
options.C: On the ground of violation of fundamental rights
options.D: On the ground of lack of jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Under Article 122, the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 118, each House of Parliament may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business. Such rules are subject to which requirement?

options.A: They must be approved by the President
options.B: They must be consistent with the Constitution
options.C: They must be approved by the Supreme Court
options.D: They must be approved by the Lok Sabha only

questions.explanation: Under Article 118, each House may make rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 120, the business of Parliament shall be transacted in which language(s)?

options.C: Hindi or English, subject to certain provisions
options.D: Any language of the Eighth Schedule

questions.explanation: Under Article 120, the business of Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English, subject to certain provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 123, the President may promulgate an Ordinance when which of the following conditions is satisfied?

options.A: At any time, even when both Houses are in session
options.B: When both Houses of Parliament are not simultaneously in session and immediate action is necessary
options.D: Only when the Lok Sabha is dissolved

questions.explanation: Under Article 123, the President may promulgate an Ordinance when both Houses of Parliament are not simultaneously in session and immediate action is necessary.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 123, an Ordinance ceases to operate at the expiration of what period after Parliament reassembles, unless approved?
questions.explanation: Under Article 123, an Ordinance ceases six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless approved or otherwise dealt with, subject to the constitutional calculation where the Houses reassemble on different dates.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 72, the President's pardoning power does NOT extend to which of the following?

options.B: Offences under laws relating to matters within Union executive power
options.D: Offences under laws relating to matters within State executive power

questions.explanation: Under Article 72, the President's pardoning power extends to court-martial cases, offences under laws relating to matters within Union executive power, and all cases of death sentence; it does not extend to offences under laws relating to matters within State executive power (that is the Governor's power under Article 161).

questions.explanation: Article 63 provides for the office of the Vice-President of India.

questions.explanation: Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.explanation: Article 81 deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha.

questions.explanation: Article 83 provides for the duration of the Houses of Parliament.

questions.explanation: Article 84 prescribes qualifications for membership of Parliament.

questions.explanation: Article 85 deals with sessions, prorogation and dissolution of Parliament.

questions.explanation: Article 86 provides for the President's right to address and send messages to Parliament.

questions.explanation: Article 87 provides for the President's special address to Parliament.

questions.question: Which Article provides for the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 89 provides for the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Which Article provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 93 provides for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which Article deals with the powers, privileges and immunities of Parliament and its members?
questions.explanation: Article 105 deals with the powers, privileges and immunities of Parliament and its members.

questions.question: Which Article provides for a joint sitting of both Houses?
questions.explanation: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of both Houses.

questions.explanation: Article 109 provides for the special procedure for Money Bills.

questions.explanation: Article 111 deals with assent to Bills.

questions.explanation: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration

questions.explanation: Article 113 deals with Demands for Grants.

questions.explanation: Article 114 provides for the Appropriation Bill.

questions.question: Which Article deals with supplementary, additional and excess grants?
questions.explanation: Article 115 deals with supplementary, additional and excess grants.

questions.question: Which Article deals with Vote on Account, Vote of Credit and Exceptional Grants?
questions.explanation: Article 116 deals with Vote on Account, Vote of Credit and Exceptional Grants.

questions.explanation: Article 118 deals with the rules of procedure of Parliament.

questions.explanation: Article 120 deals with the language to be used in Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Which Article restricts discussion in Parliament on the conduct of judges?
questions.explanation: Article 121 restricts discussion in Parliament on the conduct of judges.

questions.question: Which Article provides that courts shall not inquire into parliamentary proceedings?
questions.explanation: Article 122 provides that courts shall not inquire into parliamentary proceedings.

questions.explanation: Article 123 provides for the President's Ordinance-making power.

questions.explanation: Article 148 deals with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

questions.explanation: Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Fund and Public Account of India.

questions.explanation: Article 267 deals with the Contingency Fund of India.

questions.explanation: Article 361A protects the publication of substantially true reports of parliamentary proceedings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under the quick table of important Parliamentary Committees, the Public Accounts Committee has which composition?
questions.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under the quick table of important Parliamentary Committees, the Estimates Committee has which composition?
questions.explanation: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under the quick table of important Parliamentary Committees, the Committee on Public Undertakings has which composition?
questions.explanation: The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under the quick table of important Parliamentary Committees, Department-related Standing Committees have which composition?
questions.explanation: There are 24 Department-related Standing Committees, each with 31 members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under the quick table of important Parliamentary Committees, the Committee of Privileges has which composition?
questions.explanation: The Committee of Privileges has a House-specific composition.
