questions.question: Under the quick table of important Parliamentary Committees, the Committee on Government Assurances has which composition?
questions.explanation: The Committee on Government Assurances has a House-specific composition.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109, if a Money Bill is returned by the Rajya Sabha with recommendations, what may the Lok Sabha do?

options.A: The Lok Sabha may accept or reject all or any of the recommendations
options.B: The Lok Sabha must accept all recommendations
options.C: The Lok Sabha must reject all recommendations
options.D: The Lok Sabha must refer the Bill to a joint sitting

questions.explanation: Under Article 109, the Lok Sabha may accept or reject all or any of the recommendations made by the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109, if the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in which form?

options.A: In the form passed by the Lok Sabha
options.B: In the form passed by the Rajya Sabha
options.C: In the form recommended by the President
options.D: In the form decided by a joint sitting

questions.explanation: Under Article 109, if the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 110(3), if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, whose decision is final?

options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha's decision
options.C: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha's decision

questions.explanation: Under Article 110(3), if any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is final.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 110(3), the Speaker's certificate on a Money Bill is endorsed when the Bill is transmitted to which House?

options.A: The Rajya Sabha, when the Bill is transmitted to it
options.B: The Lok Sabha, when the Bill is introduced
options.C: Both Houses, when the Bill is presented to the President
options.D: A joint sitting, when the Bill is referred to it

questions.explanation: Under Article 110(3), the Speaker's certificate is endorsed when the Bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 117(1), a Financial Bill containing any of the matters specified in Article 110(1) along with other matters can be introduced only in which House and on whose recommendation?

options.A: Only in the Lok Sabha, on the President's recommendation
options.B: Only in the Rajya Sabha, on the Chairman's recommendation
options.C: In either House, without any recommendation

questions.explanation: Under Article 117(1), such a Financial Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 117(3), a Financial Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India can be passed only if whose recommendation has been obtained?

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 117(3), such a Financial Bill cannot be passed unless the President has recommended its consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 368, a Constitutional Amendment Bill requires ratification by at least how many State Legislatures for specified federal amendments?

options.A: At least one-fourth of the State Legislatures
options.B: At least one-third of the State Legislatures
options.C: At least half of the State Legislatures

questions.explanation: Under Article 368, specified federal amendments require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 113, the Lok Sabha may take which of the following actions on a Demand for Grant?

options.A: Assent, refuse or reduce the demand
options.B: Assent, refuse, reduce or increase the demand
options.C: Only assent or refuse the demand

questions.explanation: Under Article 113, the Lok Sabha may assent, refuse or reduce a Demand for Grant; it cannot increase it.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112, the Annual Financial Statement distinguishes expenditure on revenue account from other expenditure. What is the main purpose of this distinction?

options.A: To present the Government's estimated receipts and expenditure and communicate fiscal policy
options.B: To determine the salaries of judges
options.C: To determine the number of MPs
options.D: To determine the term of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: The Annual Financial Statement distinguishes revenue account expenditure from other expenditure as part of presenting the Government's estimated receipts and expenditure and communicating fiscal policy for the financial year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112, which of the following is NOT a purpose of the Annual Financial Statement?

options.A: To present the Government's estimated receipts and expenditure
options.B: To seek parliamentary authorisation for expenditure and taxation proposals
options.C: To communicate fiscal policy for the financial year

questions.explanation: The Annual Financial Statement presents estimated receipts and expenditure, seeks parliamentary authorisation for expenditure and taxation proposals, and communicates fiscal policy for the financial year; it does not amend the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(1), freedom of speech in Parliament is subject to which of the following?

options.A: The Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(1), freedom of speech in Parliament is subject to the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(3), the powers, privileges and immunities of each House, its members and committees are determined by whom?

options.A: Parliament by law, subject to the constitutional text and judicial interpretation

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(3), the powers, privileges and immunities of each House, its members and committees are determined by Parliament by law, subject to the constitutional text and judicial interpretation.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 54, who are the members of the President's electoral college?

options.A: The elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States, and of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and Puducherry
options.B: All members of both Houses of Parliament
options.C: The elected members of the Lok Sabha only
options.D: The members of State Legislative Councils

questions.explanation: Under Article 54, the electoral college consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States, and of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and Puducherry.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of whom?

options.A: All members of both Houses of Parliament
options.B: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament only
options.C: Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies only

questions.explanation: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of all members of both Houses of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected through which voting system?

options.A: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot
options.C: Simple majority in a joint sitting

questions.explanation: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and secret ballot.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 67, the Vice-President holds office for what period?

options.A: Five years from the date on which the Vice-President enters office
options.B: Six years from the date on which the Vice-President enters office
options.C: Four years from the date on which the Vice-President enters office
options.D: During the pleasure of the President

questions.explanation: Under Article 67, the Vice-President holds office for five years from the date on which the Vice-President enters office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 67, the Vice-President may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by what majority?

options.A: A majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.C: A two-thirds majority of the total membership
options.D: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 67, the Vice-President may be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 67, after the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution for removal of the Vice-President, what is required from the Lok Sabha?

options.B: A two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 67, the resolution for removal of the Vice-President must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(5), a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament ceases to be a Minister after what period?

options.A: Six consecutive months, unless the person becomes a member of either House

questions.explanation: Under Article 75(5), a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament ceases to be a Minister after six consecutive months, unless the person becomes a member of either House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 78, the Prime Minister must communicate to the President which of the following?

options.A: All decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals

questions.explanation: Under Article 78, the Prime Minister must communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 78, if the President requires, the Prime Minister must submit for Council consideration which of the following?

options.A: A matter decided by an individual Minister
options.B: A matter decided by the Supreme Court
options.C: A matter decided by the Speaker
options.D: A matter decided by the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 78, if the President so requires, the Prime Minister must submit for Council consideration a matter decided by an individual Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed what proportion of the total strength of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to which House?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(4), the oath of office and secrecy to Union Ministers is administered according to the forms in which Schedule?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(4), the oath of office and secrecy to Union Ministers is administered according to the forms in the Third Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 83, the Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution. What fraction of its members retire every second year?
questions.explanation: Under Article 83, as nearly as possible, one-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every second year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 83, the Lok Sabha continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved. What is the exception to this rule?

options.A: During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend its term by law for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases
options.B: During a Financial Emergency, Parliament may extend its term indefinitely
options.C: During a President's Rule, Parliament may extend its term by two years

questions.explanation: Under Article 83, during a National Emergency, Parliament may extend the term of the Lok Sabha by law for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 85, the President may from time to time prorogue which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 85, the President may from time to time prorogue either House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 85, the President may dissolve which House of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Under Article 85, the President may dissolve the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 86, the President may send messages to either House of Parliament with respect to which of the following?

options.A: A Bill then pending in Parliament or otherwise

questions.explanation: Under Article 86, the President may send messages to either House of Parliament with respect to a Bill then pending in Parliament or otherwise.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 88, who has the right to speak in, and otherwise take part in the proceedings of, either House of Parliament?

options.A: Every Minister and the Attorney-General of India

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, every Minister and the Attorney-General of India has the right to speak in, and otherwise take part in the proceedings of, either House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 88, a Minister who is not a member of a House has the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of that House, but may vote only if the Minister is a member of which House?
questions.explanation: Under Article 88, a Minister who is not a member of a House may speak in and take part in the proceedings of that House, but may vote only if the Minister is a member of that House.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 99, every member of either House of Parliament must take an oath or affirmation before taking a seat. According to which Schedule is the form of this oath or affirmation prescribed?
questions.explanation: Under Article 99, the form of the oath or affirmation is prescribed in the Third Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101, a member of either House of Parliament may resign their seat by writing to whom?

options.A: The Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be

questions.explanation: Under Article 101, a member of either House of Parliament may resign their seat by writing to the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102, a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they hold which of the following?

options.A: An office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder
options.B: A membership in a political party
options.C: A residence in a State other than their own
options.D: A teaching position in a private university

questions.explanation: Under Article 102, a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they hold an office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 103, if any question arises as to whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to any disqualification, whose decision is final?

options.A: The President's decision, after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission

questions.explanation: Under Article 103, if any question arises as to whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to any disqualification, the President's decision is final, after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 104, if a person sits or votes in either House of Parliament before taking the oath or affirmation, what penalty may be imposed?

options.A: The person shall be liable in respect of each day on which they so sit or vote to a penalty of five hundred rupees, to be recovered as a debt due to the Union
options.B: The person shall be imprisoned for six months
options.C: The person shall be disqualified for six years

questions.explanation: Under Article 104, a person who sits or votes in either House of Parliament before taking the oath or affirmation is liable to a penalty of five hundred rupees for each day, recoverable as a debt due to the Union.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 106, members of either House of Parliament are entitled to receive which of the following?

options.A: Such salaries and allowances as may be respectively fixed by Parliament by law
options.C: Salaries fixed by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 106, members of either House of Parliament are entitled to receive such salaries and allowances as may be respectively fixed by Parliament by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 107, a Bill pending in Parliament shall not lapse by reason of which of the following?

options.B: The dissolution of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The resignation of the Prime Minister
options.D: The expiry of the term of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 107, a Bill pending in Parliament shall not lapse by reason of the prorogation of the Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 107, a Bill which has been passed by the Lok Sabha and is pending in the Rajya Sabha shall lapse on dissolution of which House?
questions.explanation: Under Article 107, a Bill which has been passed by the Lok Sabha and is pending in the Rajya Sabha shall lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108, if a joint sitting is summoned, it is presided over by whom?

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then such other person as determined under the constitutional and procedural rules
options.B: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 108, a joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then such other person as determined under the constitutional and procedural rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108, a joint sitting may be summoned for the purpose of deliberating and voting on a Bill in which of the following situations?

options.A: When one House rejects the Bill, the Houses finally disagree on amendments, or more than six months elapse without passage by the other House
options.B: Only when one House rejects the Bill
options.C: Only when the Houses disagree on amendments
options.D: Only when more than one year elapses without passage

questions.explanation: Under Article 108, a joint sitting may be summoned when one House rejects the Bill, the Houses finally disagree on amendments, or more than six months elapse without passage by the other House, subject to constitutional exclusions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108, a joint sitting cannot be summoned for which of the following?

options.A: A Money Bill or a Constitutional Amendment Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 108, a joint sitting cannot be summoned for a Money Bill or a Constitutional Amendment Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 111, when a Bill is presented to the President for assent, which of the following options is available to the President in respect of a Money Bill?

options.A: The President may assent or withhold assent, but cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration
options.B: The President may assent, withhold assent, or return the Money Bill for reconsideration
options.C: The President must always assent to a Money Bill
options.D: The President may refer the Money Bill to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 111, the President may assent or withhold assent to a Money Bill, but cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112, the Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before which body?
questions.explanation: Under Article 112, the Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 113, Demands for Grants are submitted to which House for voting?
questions.explanation: Under Article 113, Demands for Grants are submitted to the Lok Sabha for voting.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 114, the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of money from which fund?
questions.explanation: Under Article 114, the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 114, the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of money to meet which of the following?

options.A: Grants voted by the Lok Sabha and expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Only grants voted by the Lok Sabha
options.C: Only expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund
options.D: Only expenditure met from the Contingency Fund

questions.explanation: Under Article 114, the Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet grants voted by the Lok Sabha and expenditure charged on the Fund.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115, a Supplementary Grant is presented to Parliament when which of the following situations arises?

options.A: When the amount authorised for a service in the current financial year is insufficient
options.B: When a new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement is required
options.C: When more money has been spent on a service than was authorised for that year
options.D: When an unforeseen expenditure needs to be met pending parliamentary authorisation

questions.explanation: Under Article 115, a Supplementary Grant is presented when the amount authorised for a service in the current financial year is insufficient.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116, a Vote on Account is granted by Parliament for what purpose?

options.A: To enable the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the full Budget process
options.B: To meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character
options.C: To meet a special purpose forming no part of the current service
options.D: To meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116, a Vote on Account is granted to enable the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the full Budget process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 266(1), all revenues received by the Government of India, all loans raised by the Government, and all moneys received by the Government in repayment of loans form which fund?
questions.explanation: Under Article 266(1), all revenues received by the Government of India, all loans raised by the Government, and all moneys received by the Government in repayment of loans form the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 266(2), all other public moneys received by or on behalf of the Government of India shall be credited to which account?
questions.explanation: Under Article 266(2), all other public moneys received by or on behalf of the Government of India shall be credited to the Public Account of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 267, the Contingency Fund of India is established by whom?

options.D: The Reserve Bank of India by regulation

questions.explanation: Under Article 267, the Contingency Fund of India is established by Parliament by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), the immunity from court proceedings extends to which of the following?

options.A: Anything said or any vote given in Parliament or a committee thereof
options.C: Any criminal act committed outside Parliament
options.D: Any act done before becoming a member

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), the immunity from court proceedings extends to anything said or any vote given in Parliament or a committee thereof.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no person is liable to proceedings in any court in respect of publication by or under the authority of either House of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), no person is liable to proceedings in any court in respect of publication by or under the authority of either House of reports, papers, votes or proceedings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 361A, protection is provided for publication of substantially true reports of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 361A, protection is provided for publication of substantially true reports of parliamentary and State Legislature proceedings, subject to its conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 59, which of the following is a condition of the President's office?

options.A: The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member is elected President, that seat becomes vacant
options.B: The President must be a member of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The President must be a member of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: The President must be a member of a State Legislature

questions.explanation: Under Article 59, the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member is elected President, that seat becomes vacant.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 59, the President is entitled to the use of which of the following without payment of rent?

options.D: A holiday home in every State

questions.explanation: Under Article 59, the President is entitled to the use of the official residence without payment of rent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 59, the emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during the President's term of office. This provision is intended to ensure what?

options.C: The supremacy of the Supreme Court
options.D: The supremacy of the Prime Minister

questions.explanation: Under Article 59, the emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during the President's term of office, which is intended to ensure the independence of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 60, the oath or affirmation is administered to the President by whom?

options.A: The Chief Justice of India; in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 60, the oath or affirmation is administered to the President by the Chief Justice of India; in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, the charge of violation of the Constitution against the President may be preferred by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 61, the charge of violation of the Constitution against the President may be preferred by either House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, the resolution for impeachment of the President must be passed by what majority of the House preferring the charge?

options.A: A majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.C: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 61, the resolution for impeachment of the President must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House preferring the charge.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, the other House that investigates the charge against the President must also pass a resolution by what majority for the President to be removed?

options.A: A majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of that House
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.C: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 61, the other House that investigates the charge must also pass a resolution by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership for the President to be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 62, an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President must be completed before which date?

options.A: Before the expiration of the term
options.B: Within six months after the expiration of the term
options.C: Within one year after the expiration of the term
options.D: Within three months after the expiration of the term

questions.explanation: Under Article 62, an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President must be completed before the expiration of the term.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 62, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of President occurring by reason of death, resignation or removal must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than what period from the date of occurrence of the vacancy?
questions.explanation: Under Article 62, an election to fill a casual vacancy must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 62, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of President serves what term?

options.A: A full five-year term from the date of entering office
options.B: The remaining portion of the predecessor's term

questions.explanation: Under Article 62, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of President serves a full five-year term from the date of entering office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 65, when the Vice-President acts as President, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of which office?

options.A: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President is entitled to which of the following?

options.A: The President's emoluments and privileges for that period

questions.explanation: Under Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President is entitled to the President's emoluments and privileges for that period.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 65, when the Vice-President is acting as President, who presides over the Rajya Sabha?

options.A: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person authorised under the rules
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 65, when the Vice-President is acting as President, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person authorised under the rules, presides over the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring by reason of the expiration of the term must be completed before which date?

options.A: Before the expiration of the term
options.B: Within six months after the expiration of the term
options.C: Within one year after the expiration of the term
options.D: Within three months after the expiration of the term

questions.explanation: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring by reason of the expiration of the term must be completed before the expiration of the term.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring by reason of death, resignation or removal must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than what period from the date of occurrence of the vacancy?
questions.explanation: Under Article 68, an election to fill a casual vacancy in the office of Vice-President must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 68, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of Vice-President serves what term?

options.A: A full five-year term from the date of entering office
options.B: The remaining portion of the predecessor's term

questions.explanation: Under Article 68, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of Vice-President serves a full five-year term from the date of entering office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 69, the oath or affirmation to the Vice-President is administered by whom?

options.A: The President, or a person appointed by the President
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 69, the oath or affirmation to the Vice-President is administered by the President, or a person appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 70, Parliament may by law make provision for the discharge of the President's functions in which of the following contingencies?

options.A: In any contingency not provided for in Articles 65 and 68
options.C: Only when the President is impeached

questions.explanation: Under Article 70, Parliament may by law make provision for the discharge of the President's functions in any contingency not provided for in Articles 65 and 68.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 71, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 71, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 71, if the election of a President or Vice-President is declared void by the Supreme Court, what happens to acts done by the person before the date of the Supreme Court's decision?

options.A: Such acts are not invalidated by reason of the declaration
options.C: Such acts require the President's approval

questions.explanation: Under Article 71, acts done by the person before the date of the Supreme Court's decision are not invalidated by reason of the declaration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 72, the President has the power to grant pardons in which of the following categories of cases?

options.A: All cases where the sentence is a sentence of death; court-martial cases; and offences against laws relating to matters within the Union executive power
options.B: Only cases where the sentence is a sentence of death

questions.explanation: Under Article 72, the President has the power to grant pardons in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death, in court-martial cases, and in offences against laws relating to matters within the Union executive power.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to which of the following?

options.A: Matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws, and to the exercise of such rights, authority and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement
options.C: Only matters relating to foreign affairs
options.D: Only matters relating to the Concurrent List

questions.explanation: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws, and to the exercise of such rights, authority and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(1), the Council of Ministers is headed by whom?

options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 74(1), the Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(2), the question whether any advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in which forum?
questions.explanation: Under Article 74(2), the question whether any advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(1), the Prime Minister is appointed by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(1), the Prime Minister is appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(2), Ministers hold office during whose pleasure?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(2), Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 80, the Rajya Sabha consists of not more than twelve members nominated by the President having special knowledge or practical experience in which fields?

options.A: Literature, science, art and social service
options.D: Agriculture, rural development, environment and forestry

questions.explanation: Under Article 80, the President nominates twelve members to the Rajya Sabha having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 84, a person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in Parliament unless they are a citizen of India and make and subscribe before a person authorised by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in which Schedule?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84, a person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in Parliament unless they are a citizen of India and make and subscribe before a person authorised by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. What happens if the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant?

options.A: The House shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be
options.C: The Rajya Sabha chooses a replacement
options.D: The office remains vacant until the next general election

questions.explanation: Under Article 93, if the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant, the House shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(3), the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House. What does 'total number of members' mean for this purpose?

options.A: The total number of members of the House, including nominated members
options.B: The total number of elected members only
options.C: The total number of members present on the day
options.D: The total number of members of the ruling party

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(3), the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, including nominated members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(4), if at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, what is the duty of the presiding officer?

options.A: It shall be the duty of the presiding officer either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum
options.B: The presiding officer shall continue the meeting
options.C: The presiding officer shall dissolve the House
options.D: The presiding officer shall refer the matter to the President

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(4), if at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the presiding officer either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101(3), if a member of either House of Parliament is absent from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission, what is the consequence?

options.A: The House may declare the seat of the member vacant
options.B: The member is automatically disqualified for six years
options.C: The member is fined five hundred rupees per day

questions.explanation: Under Article 101(3), if a member is absent from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission, the House may declare the seat of the member vacant.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they hold an office of profit under which government?

options.A: The Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder
options.C: Only the Government of a State

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified if they hold an office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(e), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they are disqualified by or under which law?

options.B: Any law made by a State Legislature
options.C: Any law made by the President
options.D: Any law made by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(e), a person shall be disqualified if they are disqualified by or under any law made by Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 103, the President shall obtain the opinion of which body before deciding whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to disqualification?
questions.explanation: Under Article 103, the President shall obtain the opinion of the Election Commission before deciding whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to disqualification.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(1), there shall be freedom of speech in Parliament. This freedom is subject to which of the following?

options.A: The Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(1), freedom of speech in Parliament is subject to the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(3), until Parliament provides by law for the powers, privileges and immunities of each House, its members and committees, what powers, privileges and immunities apply?

options.A: Those that immediately before the commencement of the Constitution were enjoyed by the House and its members, subject to the Constitution
options.C: Those prescribed by the Supreme Court
options.D: No powers, privileges or immunities apply

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(3), until Parliament provides by law, the powers, privileges and immunities are those that immediately before the commencement of the Constitution were enjoyed by the House and its members, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108, if a Bill is passed by one House and rejected by the other House, the President may summon a joint sitting of the two Houses. This joint sitting may be summoned for the purpose of doing what?

options.A: Deliberating and voting on the Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 108, a joint sitting may be summoned for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109, a Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses if the Rajya Sabha does not return it within how many days?
questions.explanation: Under Article 109, if the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 59, which of the following is a condition of the President's office?

options.A: The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member is elected President, that seat becomes vacant
options.B: The President must be a member of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The President must be a member of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: The President must be a member of a State Legislature

questions.explanation: Under Article 59, the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member is elected President, that seat becomes vacant.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 59, the President is entitled to the use of which of the following without payment of rent?

options.D: A holiday home in every State

questions.explanation: Under Article 59, the President is entitled to the use of the official residence without payment of rent.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 59, the emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during the President's term of office. This provision is intended to ensure what?

options.C: The supremacy of the Supreme Court
options.D: The supremacy of the Prime Minister

questions.explanation: Under Article 59, the emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during the President's term of office, which is intended to ensure the independence of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 60, the oath or affirmation is administered to the President by whom?

options.A: The Chief Justice of India; in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 60, the oath or affirmation is administered to the President by the Chief Justice of India; in the Chief Justice's absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, the charge of violation of the Constitution against the President may be preferred by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Under Article 61, the charge of violation of the Constitution against the President may be preferred by either House of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, the resolution for impeachment of the President must be passed by what majority of the House preferring the charge?

options.A: A majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.C: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 61, the resolution for impeachment of the President must be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House preferring the charge.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 61, the other House that investigates the charge against the President must also pass a resolution by what majority for the President to be removed?

options.A: A majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of that House
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting
options.C: A three-fourths majority of the total membership

questions.explanation: Under Article 61, the other House that investigates the charge must also pass a resolution by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership for the President to be removed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 62, an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President must be completed before which date?

options.A: Before the expiration of the term
options.B: Within six months after the expiration of the term
options.C: Within one year after the expiration of the term
options.D: Within three months after the expiration of the term

questions.explanation: Under Article 62, an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President must be completed before the expiration of the term.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 62, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of President occurring by reason of death, resignation or removal must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than what period from the date of occurrence of the vacancy?
questions.explanation: Under Article 62, an election to fill a casual vacancy must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 62, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of President serves what term?

options.A: A full five-year term from the date of entering office
options.B: The remaining portion of the predecessor's term

questions.explanation: Under Article 62, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of President serves a full five-year term from the date of entering office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 65, when the Vice-President acts as President, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of which office?

options.A: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President does not perform the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President is entitled to which of the following?

options.A: The President's emoluments and privileges for that period

questions.explanation: Under Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President is entitled to the President's emoluments and privileges for that period.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 65, when the Vice-President is acting as President, who presides over the Rajya Sabha?

options.A: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person authorised under the rules
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 65, when the Vice-President is acting as President, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person authorised under the rules, presides over the Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring by reason of the expiration of the term must be completed before which date?

options.A: Before the expiration of the term
options.B: Within six months after the expiration of the term
options.C: Within one year after the expiration of the term
options.D: Within three months after the expiration of the term

questions.explanation: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring by reason of the expiration of the term must be completed before the expiration of the term.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 68, an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President occurring by reason of death, resignation or removal must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than what period from the date of occurrence of the vacancy?
questions.explanation: Under Article 68, an election to fill a casual vacancy in the office of Vice-President must be held as soon as possible and in no case later than six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 68, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of Vice-President serves what term?

options.A: A full five-year term from the date of entering office
options.B: The remaining portion of the predecessor's term

questions.explanation: Under Article 68, a person elected to fill a casual vacancy in the office of Vice-President serves a full five-year term from the date of entering office.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 69, the oath or affirmation to the Vice-President is administered by whom?

options.A: The President, or a person appointed by the President
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 69, the oath or affirmation to the Vice-President is administered by the President, or a person appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 70, Parliament may by law make provision for the discharge of the President's functions in which of the following contingencies?

options.A: In any contingency not provided for in Articles 65 and 68
options.C: Only when the President is impeached

questions.explanation: Under Article 70, Parliament may by law make provision for the discharge of the President's functions in any contingency not provided for in Articles 65 and 68.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 71, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 71, all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 71, if the election of a President or Vice-President is declared void by the Supreme Court, what happens to acts done by the person before the date of the Supreme Court's decision?

options.A: Such acts are not invalidated by reason of the declaration
options.C: Such acts require the President's approval

questions.explanation: Under Article 71, acts done by the person before the date of the Supreme Court's decision are not invalidated by reason of the declaration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 72, the President has the power to grant pardons in which of the following categories of cases?

options.A: All cases where the sentence is a sentence of death; court-martial cases; and offences against laws relating to matters within the Union executive power
options.B: Only cases where the sentence is a sentence of death

questions.explanation: Under Article 72, the President has the power to grant pardons in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death, in court-martial cases, and in offences against laws relating to matters within the Union executive power.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to which of the following?

options.A: Matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws, and to the exercise of such rights, authority and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement
options.C: Only matters relating to foreign affairs
options.D: Only matters relating to the Concurrent List

questions.explanation: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws, and to the exercise of such rights, authority and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(1), the Council of Ministers is headed by whom?

options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 74(1), the Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(2), the question whether any advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in which forum?
questions.explanation: Under Article 74(2), the question whether any advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(1), the Prime Minister is appointed by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(1), the Prime Minister is appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(2), Ministers hold office during whose pleasure?
questions.explanation: Under Article 75(2), Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 80, the Rajya Sabha consists of not more than twelve members nominated by the President having special knowledge or practical experience in which fields?

options.A: Literature, science, art and social service
options.D: Agriculture, rural development, environment and forestry

questions.explanation: Under Article 80, the President nominates twelve members to the Rajya Sabha having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 84, a person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in Parliament unless they are a citizen of India and make and subscribe before a person authorised by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in which Schedule?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84, a person shall not be qualified to be chosen to fill a seat in Parliament unless they are a citizen of India and make and subscribe before a person authorised by the Election Commission an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. What happens if the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant?

options.A: The House shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be
options.C: The Rajya Sabha chooses a replacement
options.D: The office remains vacant until the next general election

questions.explanation: Under Article 93, if the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant, the House shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(3), the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House. What does 'total number of members' mean for this purpose?

options.A: The total number of members of the House, including nominated members
options.B: The total number of elected members only
options.C: The total number of members present on the day
options.D: The total number of members of the ruling party

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(3), the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, including nominated members.

questions.question: Under Article 100(4), if at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, what is the duty of the presiding officer?

options.A: It shall be the duty of the presiding officer either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum
options.B: The presiding officer shall continue the meeting
