questions.explanation: Under Article 100(4), if at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the presiding officer either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101(3), if a member of either House of Parliament is absent from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission, what is the consequence?

options.A: The House may declare the seat of the member vacant
options.B: The member is automatically disqualified for six years
options.C: The member is fined five hundred rupees per day

questions.explanation: Under Article 101(3), if a member is absent from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission, the House may declare the seat of the member vacant.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they hold an office of profit under which government?

options.A: The Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder
options.C: Only the Government of a State

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified if they hold an office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(e), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they are disqualified by or under which law?

options.B: Any law made by a State Legislature
options.C: Any law made by the President
options.D: Any law made by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(e), a person shall be disqualified if they are disqualified by or under any law made by Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 103, the President shall obtain the opinion of which body before deciding whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to disqualification?
questions.explanation: Under Article 103, the President shall obtain the opinion of the Election Commission before deciding whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to disqualification.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(1), there shall be freedom of speech in Parliament. This freedom is subject to which of the following?

options.A: The Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(1), freedom of speech in Parliament is subject to the Constitution and the rules and standing orders regulating parliamentary procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(3), until Parliament provides by law for the powers, privileges and immunities of each House, its members and committees, what powers, privileges and immunities apply?

options.A: Those that immediately before the commencement of the Constitution were enjoyed by the House and its members, subject to the Constitution
options.C: Those prescribed by the Supreme Court
options.D: No powers, privileges or immunities apply

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(3), until Parliament provides by law, the powers, privileges and immunities are those that immediately before the commencement of the Constitution were enjoyed by the House and its members, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108, if a Bill is passed by one House and rejected by the other House, the President may summon a joint sitting of the two Houses. This joint sitting may be summoned for the purpose of doing what?

options.A: Deliberating and voting on the Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 108, a joint sitting may be summoned for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109, a Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses if the Rajya Sabha does not return it within how many days?
questions.explanation: Under Article 109, if the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 119, Parliament may by law provide for the procedure to be followed by a joint sitting of the two Houses for the purpose of deliberating and voting on a Bill. This power is subject to which of the following?

options.C: The approval of the Supreme Court
options.D: The approval of the State Legislatures

questions.explanation: Under Article 119, Parliament may by law provide for the procedure to be followed by a joint sitting of the two Houses, subject to the provisions of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 120(1), the business in Parliament shall be transacted in which language(s)?

options.D: Any language of the Eighth Schedule

questions.explanation: Under Article 120(1), the business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 120(2), the presiding officer of a House may permit a member who cannot adequately express themselves in Hindi or English to address the House in which language?

options.B: Any language of the Eighth Schedule

questions.explanation: Under Article 120(2), the presiding officer of a House may permit a member who cannot adequately express themselves in Hindi or English to address the House in the member's mother tongue.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 121, no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties. What is the exception to this rule?

options.A: A motion for the removal of a Judge may be discussed
options.B: A motion for the appointment of a Judge may be discussed
options.C: A motion for the transfer of a Judge may be discussed

questions.explanation: Under Article 121, no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties, except upon a motion for presenting an address to the President praying for the removal of the Judge.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 122(1), the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on which ground?

options.A: On the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure
options.B: On the ground of violation of the Constitution
options.C: On the ground of violation of fundamental rights
options.D: On the ground of lack of jurisdiction

questions.explanation: Under Article 122(1), the validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 122(2), no officer or member of Parliament in whom powers are vested by or under the Constitution for regulating procedure or the conduct of business, or for maintaining order, in Parliament shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of which of the following?

options.A: The exercise by them of those powers
options.D: Any criminal act committed outside Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 122(2), no officer or member of Parliament in whom powers are vested for regulating procedure or the conduct of business, or for maintaining order, shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise by them of those powers.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 123(1), the President may promulgate an Ordinance when which of the following conditions is satisfied?

options.A: At any time when both Houses of Parliament are not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action
options.B: Only when both Houses are in session
options.D: Only when the Lok Sabha is dissolved

questions.explanation: Under Article 123(1), the President may promulgate an Ordinance when both Houses of Parliament are not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it necessary for him to take immediate action.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 123(2), an Ordinance promulgated by the President shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament. What happens to the Ordinance if it is not approved by Parliament?

options.A: It ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament
options.D: It is automatically extended by six months

questions.explanation: Under Article 123(2), an Ordinance shall cease to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament, or, if before the expiration of that period resolutions disapproving it are passed by both Houses, upon the passing of the second of those resolutions.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 123(2), if the Houses of Parliament are reassembled on different dates, what is the period of six weeks calculated from?

options.C: The date of the first House's reassembly
options.D: The date of the President's promulgation

questions.explanation: Under Article 123(2), if the Houses of Parliament are reassembled on different dates, the period of six weeks is calculated from the later of those dates.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 123(3), an Ordinance may be withdrawn at any time by the President. What is the consequence of such withdrawal?

options.A: The Ordinance ceases to operate from the date of withdrawal
options.B: The Ordinance continues for six weeks
options.C: The Ordinance becomes a permanent Act
options.D: The Ordinance is referred to Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 123(3), an Ordinance may be withdrawn at any time by the President, and it ceases to operate from the date of withdrawal.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 72(1), the President has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offence in which of the following categories of cases?

options.A: In all cases where the punishment or sentence is by a court-martial; in all cases where the punishment or sentence is for an offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends; and in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death
options.B: Only in cases where the sentence is a sentence of death
options.D: Only in cases relating to State laws

questions.explanation: Under Article 72(1), the President has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence in all court-martial cases, in all cases where the punishment or sentence is for an offence against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends, and in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 72(3), the President shall not exercise the power of granting pardons in which of the following cases?

options.A: In cases where the sentence is for an offence against a law relating to a matter to which the executive power of a State extends
options.B: In cases where the sentence is a sentence of death
options.D: In cases relating to Union laws

questions.explanation: Under Article 72(3), the President shall not exercise the power of granting pardons in cases where the sentence is for an offence against a law relating to a matter to which the executive power of a State extends; that power belongs to the Governor under Article 161.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(1), the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice. What is the consequence if the President requires such reconsideration?

options.A: The President must act in accordance with the advice tendered after reconsideration
options.C: The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha
options.D: The President may refer the matter to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under the proviso to Article 74(1), the President may require the Council of Ministers to reconsider its advice, but must act in accordance with the advice tendered after reconsideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 74(2), the question whether any advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in which forum?
questions.explanation: Under Article 74(2), the question whether any advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. This provision was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 introduced the 15 per cent ceiling on the Union Council of Ministers under Article 75(1A).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha. Does this cap include the Prime Minister?

options.A: Yes, the cap includes the Prime Minister
options.B: No, the Prime Minister is excluded
options.C: Only if the Prime Minister is a Lok Sabha member

questions.explanation: Under Article 75(1A), the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, cannot exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 75(5), a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament must become a member of either House within six consecutive months. What happens if the Minister fails to become a member within this period?

options.A: The Minister ceases to be a Minister
options.C: The Minister is automatically elected to the Lok Sabha
options.D: The Minister is automatically elected to the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 75(5), a Minister who is not a member of either House of Parliament must become a member within six consecutive months or cease to be a Minister.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 76(1), the Attorney-General for India is appointed by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 76(1), the Attorney-General for India is appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 76(1), a person shall not be qualified to be appointed as Attorney-General for India unless they are qualified to be appointed as a Judge of which court?
questions.explanation: Under Article 76(1), a person shall not be qualified to be appointed as Attorney-General for India unless they are qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 76(2), it is the duty of the Attorney-General for India to give advice to the Government of India upon such legal matters, and to perform such other duties of a legal character, as may from time to time be referred or assigned to him by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 76(2), it is the duty of the Attorney-General for India to give advice to the Government of India upon such legal matters, and to perform such other duties of a legal character, as may from time to time be referred or assigned to him by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 76(4), the Attorney-General for India shall hold office during whose pleasure?
questions.explanation: Under Article 76(4), the Attorney-General for India shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 77(1), all executive action of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in whose name?
questions.explanation: Under Article 77(1), all executive action of the Government of India shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 77(2), orders and other instruments made and executed in the name of the President shall be authenticated in such manner as may be specified in rules to be made by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 77(2), orders and other instruments made and executed in the name of the President shall be authenticated in such manner as may be specified in rules to be made by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 77(3), the President shall make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India, and for the allocation among Ministers of the said business. What is the purpose of such rules?

options.A: To ensure the convenient transaction of business and allocation of business among Ministers

questions.explanation: Under Article 77(3), the President shall make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the Government of India, and for the allocation among Ministers of the said business.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 78(a), it is the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation. What is the purpose of this duty?

options.A: To keep the President informed of the decisions of the Council of Ministers

questions.explanation: Under Article 78(a), it is the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation, so as to keep the President informed.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 78(b), it is the duty of the Prime Minister to furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation as whom may call for?
questions.explanation: Under Article 78(b), it is the duty of the Prime Minister to furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the Union and proposals for legislation as the President may call for.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 78(c), if the President so requires, it is the duty of the Prime Minister to submit for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter on which a decision has been taken by a Minister but which has not been considered by the Council. What is the purpose of this duty?

options.A: To ensure collective consideration of matters decided by individual Ministers

questions.explanation: Under Article 78(c), if the President so requires, it is the duty of the Prime Minister to submit for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter on which a decision has been taken by a Minister but which has not been considered by the Council, so as to ensure collective consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of which of the following?

options.A: The President and two Houses, namely the Council of States and the House of the People

questions.explanation: Under Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of the President and two Houses, namely the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 80(1)(a), the Council of States shall consist of not more than how many representatives of the States and Union Territories?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80(1)(a), the Council of States shall consist of not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 80(1)(b), the Council of States shall consist of how many members nominated by the President?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80(1)(b), the Council of States shall consist of twelve members nominated by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 80(3), the twelve members nominated by the President to the Council of States shall be persons having special knowledge or practical experience in which fields?

options.A: Literature, science, art and social service
options.D: Agriculture, rural development, environment and forestry

questions.explanation: Under Article 80(3), the twelve members nominated by the President shall be persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 81(1)(a), the House of the People shall consist of not more than how many members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States?
questions.explanation: Under Article 81(1)(a), the House of the People shall consist of not more than 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 81(1)(b), the House of the People shall consist of not more than how many members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Union Territories?
questions.explanation: Under Article 81(1)(b), the House of the People shall consist of not more than 20 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the Union Territories.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 83(1), the Council of States shall not be subject to dissolution. What is the term of office of a member of the Council of States?
questions.explanation: Under Article 83(1), the Council of States shall not be subject to dissolution, and the term of office of a member is six years, with approximately one-third retiring every second year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 83(2), the House of the People shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting. What is the exception to this rule?

options.A: During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend its term by law for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases
options.B: During a Financial Emergency, Parliament may extend its term indefinitely
options.C: During a President's Rule, Parliament may extend its term by two years

questions.explanation: Under Article 83(2), during a National Emergency, Parliament may extend the term of the House of the People by law for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 85(1), the President shall summon each House of Parliament at such time and place as he thinks fit, but so that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. What is the consequence of this provision?

options.A: Parliament must meet at least twice a year
options.B: Parliament must meet at least once a year
options.C: Parliament must meet at least four times a year

questions.explanation: Under Article 85(1), six months shall not intervene between the last sitting in one session and the first sitting in the next session, which effectively requires Parliament to meet at least twice a year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 85(2), the President may from time to time prorogue the Houses or either House, and dissolve which House?
questions.explanation: Under Article 85(2), the President may from time to time prorogue the Houses or either House, and dissolve the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 86(1), the President may address either House of Parliament or both Houses assembled together, and for that purpose require the attendance of members. What is the purpose of such an address?

options.A: To address either House or both Houses assembled together

questions.explanation: Under Article 86(1), the President may address either House of Parliament or both Houses assembled together, and for that purpose require the attendance of members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 87(1), the President shall address both Houses of Parliament assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the House of the People. What is the purpose of this address?

options.A: To inform Parliament of the causes of its summons

questions.explanation: Under Article 87(1), the President shall address both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the commencement of the first session of each year, to inform Parliament of the causes of its summons.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 87(2), provision shall be made by the rules regulating the procedure of either House for the allotment of time for the discussion of which of the following?

options.A: The matters referred to in the President's address

questions.explanation: Under Article 87(2), provision shall be made by the rules regulating the procedure of either House for the allotment of time for the discussion of the matters referred to in the President's address.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 88, every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise take part in the proceedings of, either House, any joint sitting of the Houses, and any committee of Parliament of which they may be named a member. What is the limitation on this right?

options.A: They shall not by virtue of this Article be entitled to vote
options.B: They may vote in either House
options.C: They may vote in a joint sitting
options.D: They may vote in a committee

questions.explanation: Under Article 88, every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in and otherwise take part in the proceedings of either House, any joint sitting, and any committee of Parliament of which they may be named a member, but shall not by virtue of this Article be entitled to vote.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 89(1), the Vice-President of India shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States. What is the consequence of the Vice-President acting as President under Article 65?

options.A: The Vice-President shall not perform the duties of the office of Chairman of the Council of States
options.B: The Vice-President shall continue to perform the duties of Chairman
options.C: The Vice-President shall be replaced by the Deputy Chairman
options.D: The Vice-President shall resign as Chairman

questions.explanation: Under Article 89(1) read with Article 65, while acting as President, the Vice-President shall not perform the duties of the office of Chairman of the Council of States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 89(2), the Council of States shall, as soon as may be, choose a member of the Council to be Deputy Chairman. What happens if the office of Deputy Chairman becomes vacant?

options.A: The Council shall choose another member to be Deputy Chairman

questions.explanation: Under Article 89(2), if the office of Deputy Chairman becomes vacant, the Council shall choose another member to be Deputy Chairman.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 90, the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States may be removed from office by a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council. What notice period is required for such a resolution?
questions.explanation: Under Article 90, at least 14 days' notice is required for a resolution to remove the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 91(1), while the office of Chairman is vacant, or during any period when the Vice-President is acting as President, the duties of the office of Chairman shall be performed by whom?

options.A: The Deputy Chairman, or, if that office is also vacant, by such member of the Council as the President may appoint for the purpose
options.B: The Speaker of the House of the People

questions.explanation: Under Article 91(1), while the office of Chairman is vacant or during any period when the Vice-President is acting as President, the duties of the office of Chairman shall be performed by the Deputy Chairman, or, if that office is also vacant, by such member of the Council as the President may appoint for the purpose.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 92, the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of the Council of States shall not be removed from office except by a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council. What is the exception to this rule?

options.A: The Chairman may be removed from office by a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council
options.B: The Chairman may be removed by the President
options.C: The Chairman may be removed by the House of the People
options.D: The Chairman may be removed by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 92, the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of the Council of States shall not be removed from office except by a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 93, the House of the People shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the House to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker. What happens if the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant?

options.A: The House shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be
options.C: The Council of States chooses a replacement
options.D: The office remains vacant until the next general election

questions.explanation: Under Article 93, if the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant, the House shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 94, the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the House of the People shall not be removed from office except by a resolution of the House passed by a majority of all the then members of the House. What notice period is required for such a resolution?
questions.explanation: Under Article 94, at least 14 days' notice is required for a resolution to remove the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 95(1), while the office of Speaker is vacant, the duties of the office shall be performed by whom?

options.A: The Deputy Speaker, or, if that office is also vacant, by such member of the House as the President may appoint for the purpose
options.B: The Chairman of the Council of States

questions.explanation: Under Article 95(1), while the office of Speaker is vacant, the duties of the office shall be performed by the Deputy Speaker, or, if that office is also vacant, by such member of the House as the President may appoint for the purpose.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 96, the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the House of the People shall not preside over a sitting of the House while a resolution for their removal from office is under consideration. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To ensure an impartial presiding officer during the removal proceedings
options.B: To allow the Speaker to vote on the resolution
options.C: To allow the Deputy Speaker to preside over the proceedings
options.D: To allow the President to preside over the proceedings

questions.explanation: Under Article 96, the Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall not preside over a sitting of the House while a resolution for their removal is under consideration, so as to ensure an impartial presiding officer during the removal proceedings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 97, the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People shall be fixed by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 97, the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People shall be fixed by Parliament by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 98, each House of Parliament shall have a separate secretarial staff. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To ensure that each House has its own independent secretarial staff
options.B: To reduce the cost of Parliament
options.C: To allow the President to control the staff
options.D: To allow the Prime Minister to control the staff

questions.explanation: Under Article 98, each House of Parliament shall have a separate secretarial staff, so as to ensure that each House has its own independent secretarial staff.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 99, every member of either House of Parliament shall, before taking their seat, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in which Schedule?
questions.explanation: Under Article 99, every member of either House of Parliament shall make and subscribe an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(3), the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House. What does 'total number of members' mean for this purpose?

options.A: The total number of members of the House, including nominated members
options.B: The total number of elected members only
options.C: The total number of members present on the day
options.D: The total number of members of the ruling party

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(3), the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, including nominated members.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 100(4), if at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the presiding officer to do which of the following?

options.A: Either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum
options.D: To refer the matter to the President

questions.explanation: Under Article 100(4), if at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the presiding officer either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101(1), no person shall be a member of both Houses of Parliament. What happens if a person is elected to both Houses?

options.A: The person's seat in one House shall become vacant as provided by law made by Parliament
options.B: The person may continue as a member of both Houses
options.C: The person must resign from both Houses
options.D: The person may choose which House to remain a member of

questions.explanation: Under Article 101(1), no person shall be a member of both Houses of Parliament, and if a person is elected to both Houses, the person's seat in one House shall become vacant as provided by law made by Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101(2), no person shall be a member of both Houses of Parliament and of a House of the Legislature of a State. What happens if a person is elected to both?

options.A: The person's seat in Parliament shall become vacant as provided by law made by Parliament
options.B: The person may continue as a member of both
options.C: The person must resign from both
options.D: The person may choose which House to remain a member of

questions.explanation: Under Article 101(2), no person shall be a member of both Houses of Parliament and of a House of the Legislature of a State, and if a person is elected to both, the person's seat in Parliament shall become vacant as provided by law made by Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101(3)(a), if a member of either House of Parliament resigns their seat, to whom must the resignation be addressed?

options.A: The Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be

questions.explanation: Under Article 101(3)(a), a member of either House of Parliament may resign their seat by writing to the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 101(3)(b), if a member of either House of Parliament is absent from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission, what is the consequence?

options.A: The House may declare the seat of the member vacant
options.B: The member is automatically disqualified for six years
options.C: The member is fined five hundred rupees per day

questions.explanation: Under Article 101(3)(b), if a member is absent from all meetings of the House for a period of sixty days without permission, the House may declare the seat of the member vacant.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they hold an office of profit under which government?

options.A: The Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder
options.C: Only the Government of a State

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(a), a person shall be disqualified if they hold an office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(b), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they are of unsound mind and stand so declared by which authority?
questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(b), a person shall be disqualified if they are of unsound mind and stand so declared by a competent court.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(c), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they are an undischarged insolvent. What is the meaning of 'undischarged insolvent'?

options.A: A person who has been declared insolvent and has not been discharged
options.B: A person who has been declared bankrupt and has been discharged
options.C: A person who has never been declared insolvent
options.D: A person who has been declared insolvent and has been discharged

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(c), a person shall be disqualified if they are an undischarged insolvent, that is, a person who has been declared insolvent and has not been discharged.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(d), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they cease to be a citizen of India, or have voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State, or are under any acknowledgment of allegiance or adherence to a foreign State. What is the consequence of such disqualification?

options.A: The person is disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament
options.B: The person is disqualified for six years
options.C: The person is fined five hundred rupees per day
options.D: The person is imprisoned for six months

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(d), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they cease to be a citizen of India, or have voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State, or are under any acknowledgment of allegiance or adherence to a foreign State.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 102(1)(e), a person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament if they are disqualified by or under which law?

options.B: Any law made by a State Legislature
options.C: Any law made by the President
options.D: Any law made by the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 102(1)(e), a person shall be disqualified if they are disqualified by or under any law made by Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 103(1), if any question arises as to whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in Article 102(1), whose decision is final?
questions.explanation: Under Article 103(1), if any question arises as to whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in Article 102(1), the President's decision is final.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 103(2), before giving a decision on a question of disqualification of a member of either House of Parliament, the President shall obtain the opinion of which body?
questions.explanation: Under Article 103(2), before giving a decision on a question of disqualification, the President shall obtain the opinion of the Election Commission.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 104, if a person sits or votes in either House of Parliament before taking the oath or affirmation, what penalty may be imposed?

options.A: The person shall be liable in respect of each day on which they so sit or vote to a penalty of five hundred rupees, to be recovered as a debt due to the Union
options.B: The person shall be imprisoned for six months
options.C: The person shall be disqualified for six years

questions.explanation: Under Article 104, a person who sits or votes in either House of Parliament before taking the oath or affirmation is liable to a penalty of five hundred rupees for each day, recoverable as a debt due to the Union.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(1), there shall be freedom of speech in Parliament. What is the scope of this freedom?

options.A: Subject to the provisions of the Constitution and to the rules and standing orders regulating the procedure of Parliament
options.C: Subject only to the President's approval
options.D: Subject only to the Supreme Court's approval

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(1), there shall be freedom of speech in Parliament, subject to the provisions of the Constitution and to the rules and standing orders regulating the procedure of Parliament.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no member of Parliament shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by them in Parliament or any committee thereof. What is the scope of this immunity?

options.A: It extends to anything said or any vote given in Parliament or any committee thereof
options.B: It extends to any statement made outside Parliament
options.C: It extends to any criminal act committed outside Parliament
options.D: It extends to any act done before becoming a member

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), no member of Parliament shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by them in Parliament or any committee thereof.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no person shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of the publication by or under the authority of either House of Parliament of any report, paper, votes or proceedings. What is the scope of this immunity?

options.A: It extends to publication by or under the authority of either House of Parliament of any report, paper, votes or proceedings
options.B: It extends to any publication in a newspaper
options.C: It extends to any book written by a member
options.D: It extends to any speech made outside Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), no person shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of the publication by or under the authority of either House of Parliament of any report, paper, votes or proceedings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(3), until Parliament provides by law for the powers, privileges and immunities of each House, its members and committees, what powers, privileges and immunities apply?

options.A: Those that immediately before the commencement of the Constitution were enjoyed by the House and its members, subject to the Constitution
options.C: Those prescribed by the Supreme Court
options.D: No powers, privileges or immunities apply

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(3), until Parliament provides by law, the powers, privileges and immunities are those that immediately before the commencement of the Constitution were enjoyed by the House and its members, subject to the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 106, members of either House of Parliament are entitled to receive such salaries and allowances as may be respectively fixed by Parliament by law. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To ensure that members receive salaries and allowances as fixed by Parliament
options.B: To allow the President to fix salaries
options.C: To allow the Supreme Court to fix salaries
options.D: To allow the Council of Ministers to fix salaries

questions.explanation: Under Article 106, members of either House of Parliament are entitled to receive such salaries and allowances as may be respectively fixed by Parliament by law.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 107(1), a Bill pending in Parliament shall not lapse by reason of the prorogation of the Houses. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To ensure that a Bill pending in Parliament does not lapse on prorogation
options.B: To allow the President to withdraw the Bill
options.C: To allow the Speaker to withdraw the Bill
options.D: To allow the Prime Minister to withdraw the Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 107(1), a Bill pending in Parliament shall not lapse by reason of the prorogation of the Houses.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 107(3), a Bill which has been passed by the Council of States and is pending in the House of the People shall lapse on dissolution of which House?
questions.explanation: Under Article 107(3), a Bill which has been passed by the Council of States and is pending in the House of the People shall lapse on dissolution of the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 107(4), a Bill which has been passed by both Houses and is awaiting assent of the President shall not lapse on dissolution of the House of the People. What is the consequence of this provision?

options.A: The Bill does not lapse and may be proceeded with
options.C: The Bill requires the President's approval to proceed
options.D: The Bill requires a joint sitting to proceed

questions.explanation: Under Article 107(4), a Bill which has been passed by both Houses and is awaiting assent of the President shall not lapse on dissolution of the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108(1), if a Bill has been passed by one House and transmitted to the other House and the other House rejects the Bill, the President may summon a joint sitting. What is the purpose of such a joint sitting?

options.A: To deliberate and vote on the Bill
options.D: To dissolve the House of the People

questions.explanation: Under Article 108(1), if a Bill has been passed by one House and transmitted to the other House and the other House rejects the Bill, the President may summon a joint sitting for the purpose of deliberating and voting on the Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108(1), a joint sitting may be summoned if more than six months elapse from the date of the reception of the Bill by the other House without the Bill being passed by it. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To resolve a deadlock when the other House fails to pass the Bill within six months
options.B: To allow the President to withdraw the Bill
options.C: To allow the Speaker to withdraw the Bill
options.D: To allow the Prime Minister to withdraw the Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 108(1), a joint sitting may be summoned if more than six months elapse from the date of the reception of the Bill by the other House without the Bill being passed by it, so as to resolve a deadlock.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108(1), a joint sitting cannot be summoned for which of the following types of Bills?

options.A: A Money Bill or a Constitutional Amendment Bill

questions.explanation: Under Article 108(1), a joint sitting cannot be summoned for a Money Bill or a Constitutional Amendment Bill.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 108(2), when a joint sitting is summoned, it shall be presided over by whom?

options.A: The Speaker of the House of the People; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then such other person as determined under the constitutional and procedural rules
options.B: The Chairman of the Council of States

questions.explanation: Under Article 108(2), a joint sitting shall be presided over by the Speaker of the House of the People; in the Speaker's absence, the Deputy Speaker, and then such other person as determined under the constitutional and procedural rules.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109(1), a Money Bill shall be introduced only in which House?
questions.explanation: Under Article 109(1), a Money Bill shall be introduced only in the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109(2), after a Money Bill has been passed by the House of the People, it shall be transmitted to the Council of States for its recommendations. What is the time limit for the Council of States to return the Bill?

options.A: Within 14 days from the date of its receipt
options.B: Within 7 days from the date of its receipt
options.C: Within 21 days from the date of its receipt
options.D: Within 30 days from the date of its receipt

questions.explanation: Under Article 109(2), the Council of States shall return the Money Bill within 14 days from the date of its receipt.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109(3), if the Council of States does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses. What is the form in which the Bill is deemed to have been passed?

options.A: In the form in which it was passed by the House of the People
options.B: In the form recommended by the Council of States
options.C: In the form recommended by the President
options.D: In the form decided by a joint sitting

questions.explanation: Under Article 109(3), if the Council of States does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, the Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form in which it was passed by the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109(4), when a Money Bill is returned to the House of the People with the recommendations of the Council of States, what may the House of the People do?

options.A: The House of the People may accept or reject all or any of the recommendations
options.B: The House of the People must accept all recommendations
options.C: The House of the People must reject all recommendations
options.D: The House of the People must refer the Bill to a joint sitting

questions.explanation: Under Article 109(4), the House of the People may accept or reject all or any of the recommendations made by the Council of States.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 109(5), when a Money Bill is returned to the House of the People with recommendations of the Council of States, the Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses in which form?

options.A: In the form in which it was passed by the House of the People, with such amendments as are recommended by the Council of States and accepted by the House of the People
options.B: In the form recommended by the Council of States
options.C: In the form recommended by the President
options.D: In the form decided by a joint sitting

questions.explanation: Under Article 109(5), the Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form in which it was passed by the House of the People, with such amendments as are recommended by the Council of States and accepted by the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 110(1), a Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with any of the matters specified in clauses (a) to (g). What is the consequence of a Bill containing provisions dealing with matters other than those specified?

options.A: The Bill is not a Money Bill
options.B: The Bill is still a Money Bill
options.C: The Bill is referred to the President
options.D: The Bill is referred to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 110(1), a Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill only if it contains only provisions dealing with the matters specified in clauses (a) to (g).

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 111, when a Bill is presented to the President for assent, the President may declare that he assents to the Bill, or that he withholds assent therefrom, or that he returns the Bill to the Houses for reconsideration. What is the consequence of the President returning a Bill other than a Money Bill for reconsideration?

options.A: The Houses shall reconsider the Bill, and if it is passed again by both Houses with or without amendment and presented to the President for assent, the President shall not withhold assent therefrom
options.D: The Bill is referred to the Supreme Court

questions.explanation: Under Article 111, if the President returns a Bill other than a Money Bill for reconsideration, the Houses shall reconsider the Bill, and if it is passed again by both Houses with or without amendment and presented to the President for assent, the President shall not withhold assent therefrom.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(1), the President shall cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament the Annual Financial Statement. What is the purpose of this Statement?

options.A: To show the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for the financial year

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(1), the Annual Financial Statement is caused to be laid before both Houses of Parliament to show the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for the financial year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), the following expenditure shall be expenditure charged on the revenues of India. Which of the following is included?

options.A: The salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of Judges of the Supreme Court
options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), the salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of Judges of the Supreme Court are charged on the revenues of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 112(3), the following expenditure shall be expenditure charged on the revenues of India. Which of the following is included?

options.A: The salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
options.B: The salary of a clerk in a ministry
options.C: The cost of a new highway
options.D: The salary of a state government employee

questions.explanation: Under Article 112(3), the salaries, allowances and pensions payable to or in respect of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India are charged on the revenues of India.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 113(1), the estimates of expenditure embodied in the Annual Financial Statement shall show separately the expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and the expenditure proposed to be made from the Consolidated Fund of India. What is the purpose of this distinction?

options.A: To distinguish between expenditure that is not voted upon and expenditure that is voted upon
options.B: To distinguish between revenue and capital expenditure
options.C: To distinguish between defence and development expenditure
options.D: To distinguish between Union and State expenditure

questions.explanation: Under Article 113(1), the estimates of expenditure shall show separately the expenditure charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and the expenditure proposed to be made from the Consolidated Fund of India, so as to distinguish between expenditure that is not voted upon and expenditure that is voted upon.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 114(1), the President shall, after the Demands for Grants are voted by the House of the People, introduce an Appropriation Bill. What is the purpose of the Appropriation Bill?

options.A: To authorise the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants voted by the House of the People and the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund
options.B: To give effect to taxation proposals

questions.explanation: Under Article 114(1), the Appropriation Bill authorises the withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants voted by the House of the People and the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 114(3), no money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law passed in accordance with the provisions of which Article?
questions.explanation: Under Article 114(3), no money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law passed in accordance with the provisions of Article 114.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115(1)(a), a Supplementary Grant is sought when the amount authorised by law to be expended for a particular service for the current financial year is found to be insufficient for the purposes of that year. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To allow the Government to seek additional funds when the authorised amount is insufficient
options.B: To allow the Government to seek funds for a new service
options.C: To allow the Government to seek funds for expenditure in excess of the amount granted
options.D: To allow the Government to seek funds for an unforeseen expenditure

questions.explanation: Under Article 115(1)(a), a Supplementary Grant is sought when the amount authorised by law to be expended for a particular service for the current financial year is found to be insufficient for the purposes of that year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115(1)(b), an Additional Grant is sought when a need has arisen for expenditure upon some new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement for that year. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To allow the Government to seek funds for a new service
options.B: To allow the Government to seek additional funds when the authorised amount is insufficient
options.C: To allow the Government to seek funds for expenditure in excess of the amount granted
options.D: To allow the Government to seek funds for an unforeseen expenditure

questions.explanation: Under Article 115(1)(b), an Additional Grant is sought when a need has arisen for expenditure upon some new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement for that year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 115(1)(c), an Excess Grant is sought when any money has been spent on any service during a financial year in excess of the amount granted for that service. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To allow the Government to seek funds for expenditure in excess of the amount granted
options.B: To allow the Government to seek additional funds when the authorised amount is insufficient
options.C: To allow the Government to seek funds for a new service
options.D: To allow the Government to seek funds for an unforeseen expenditure

questions.explanation: Under Article 115(1)(c), an Excess Grant is sought when any money has been spent on any service during a financial year in excess of the amount granted for that service.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116(1)(a), a Vote on Account is granted when the President is satisfied that it is necessary to make a grant in advance for the estimated expenditure for part of a financial year pending the completion of the procedure prescribed in Articles 113 and 114. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To allow the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the full Budget process
options.B: To allow the Government to meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character
options.C: To allow the Government to meet a special purpose forming no part of the current service
options.D: To allow the Government to meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116(1)(a), a Vote on Account is granted to allow the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the full Budget process.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116(1)(b), a Vote of Credit is granted when the President is satisfied that owing to the magnitude or indefinite character of the service, the expenditure cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Budget. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To allow the Government to meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character
options.B: To allow the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year
options.C: To allow the Government to meet a special purpose forming no part of the current service
options.D: To allow the Government to meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116(1)(b), a Vote of Credit is granted to allow the Government to meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 116(1)(c), an Exceptional Grant is granted for a special purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To allow the Government to meet a special purpose forming no part of the current service
options.B: To allow the Government to meet expenditure for part of a financial year
options.C: To allow the Government to meet an unexpected demand of indefinite character
options.D: To allow the Government to meet expenditure when the amount authorised for a service is insufficient

questions.explanation: Under Article 116(1)(c), an Exceptional Grant is granted for a special purpose forming no part of the current service of any financial year.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 117(1), a Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters specified in Article 110(1)(a) to (f) shall not be introduced or moved in the Council of States. What is the consequence of this provision?

options.A: Such a Bill or amendment can be introduced or moved only in the House of the People
options.B: Such a Bill or amendment can be introduced or moved in either House
options.C: Such a Bill or amendment can be introduced or moved only in a joint sitting
options.D: Such a Bill or amendment cannot be introduced or moved at all

questions.explanation: Under Article 117(1), a Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters specified in Article 110(1)(a) to (f) shall not be introduced or moved in the Council of States, and can be introduced or moved only in the House of the People.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 117(3), a Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India shall not be passed by either House of Parliament unless the President has recommended its consideration. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To ensure that the President's recommendation is obtained before passing a Bill involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund
options.B: To ensure that the Speaker's recommendation is obtained
options.C: To ensure that the Prime Minister's recommendation is obtained
options.D: To ensure that the Supreme Court's approval is obtained

questions.explanation: Under Article 117(3), a Bill which, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India shall not be passed by either House of Parliament unless the President has recommended its consideration.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no member of Parliament shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said or any vote given by them in Parliament or any committee thereof. What is the scope of this immunity?

options.A: It extends to anything said or any vote given in Parliament or any committee thereof
options.B: It extends to any statement made outside Parliament
options.C: It extends to any criminal act committed outside Parliament
options.D: It extends to any act done before becoming a member

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), the immunity extends to anything said or any vote given in Parliament or any committee thereof.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 105(2), no person shall be liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of the publication by or under the authority of either House of Parliament of any report, paper, votes or proceedings. What is the scope of this immunity?

options.A: It extends to publication by or under the authority of either House of Parliament of any report, paper, votes or proceedings
options.B: It extends to any publication in a newspaper
options.C: It extends to any book written by a member
options.D: It extends to any speech made outside Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 105(2), the immunity extends to publication by or under the authority of either House of Parliament of any report, paper, votes or proceedings.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 361A(1), no person shall be liable to any proceedings, civil or criminal, in any court in respect of the publication in a newspaper of a substantially true report of any proceedings of either House of Parliament or the Legislative Assembly, or, as the case may be, either House of the Legislature, of a State, unless the publication is proved to have been made with malice. What is the purpose of this provision?

options.A: To protect the publication of substantially true reports of parliamentary and State Legislature proceedings
options.B: To protect the publication of any newspaper article
options.C: To protect the publication of any book written by a member
options.D: To protect the publication of any speech made outside Parliament

questions.explanation: Under Article 361A(1), the purpose of this provision is to protect the publication of substantially true reports of parliamentary and State Legislature proceedings, unless the publication is proved to have been made with malice.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution and Public Administration
questions.question: Under Article 361A(2), the protection of Article 361A(1) shall not apply to the publication of any report of the proceedings of a secret sitting of either House of Parliament or the Legislature of a State. What is the consequence of this exception?

options.A: Publication of reports of secret sittings is not protected by Article 361A
options.B: Publication of reports of secret sittings is protected by Article 105
options.C: Publication of reports of secret sittings is protected by Article 194
options.D: Publication of reports of secret sittings is protected by Article 122

questions.explanation: Under Article 361A(2), the protection of Article 361A(1) does not apply to the publication of any report of the proceedings of a secret sitting of either House of Parliament or the Legislature of a State.
